✦ WorkspaceAssistant Full

Tutorial

Architect an On-Device AI Agent

Build the complete Workspace Assistant: a task app whose on-device assistant changes your workspace through the same commands you use, with undo for everything, data saved with SwiftData, and tests that run without a model. These tutorials follow the app's core path; supporting views and the design system come ready-made in the project download.

Get started

Chapter 1

The Domain

Model tasks, describe every change as a command, and build the single store that applies commands, saves them and undoes them.

Tutorial 1 · 20 minModelling the WorkspaceStart with plain Swift values: tasks, their categories and steps, and a single enum that lists every change the app can make. Nothing here imports SwiftUI, SwiftData or FoundationModels, which is what makes the rest easy to test.Tutorial 2 · 35 minThe Store and UndoBuild WorkspaceStore, the single source of truth. It applies commands, keeps tasks in order, saves through a protocol, records who changed what, and registers an undo for every change, including the assistant's.Tutorial 3 · 20 minSaving with SwiftDataImplement the store's storage protocols. Tasks are saved with SwiftData through a storage model that mirrors TaskItem; preferences go to UserDefaults. Then create the composition root that decides which implementations the app uses.

Chapter 2

The Interface

Give the board a view model, add the design system, and put four animated layouts on screen.

Tutorial 4 · 30 minView Models and the BoardGive the board a view model that turns taps into commands, add the ready-made design system, and put the board on screen with four layouts that animate every change.

Chapter 3

The Assistant

Turn the store into nine tools, run them with Apple Intelligence or a scripted stand-in, show every step in a chat, and test it all without a model.

Tutorial 5 · 30 minTools and the ToolboxGive the assistant hands. A toolbox resolves the model's words to tasks, performs commands as the assistant, and reports exactly what happened. Nine thin tools expose it to Foundation Models.Tutorial 6 · 30 minThe Assistant EngineHide the language model behind a protocol. The real engine keeps one long-lived Foundation Models session and streams events as it works; a scripted engine stands in when Apple Intelligence isn't available, and an automatic engine chooses between them on every prompt.Tutorial 7 · 25 minThe Assistant PanelTurn the engine's event stream into a conversation: user messages, action blocks for every tool call, and a reply that streams in. Then connect the assistant to the app, with a pill above the tab bar that opens it over the live board.Tutorial 8 · 25 minTesting Without a ModelBecause every behaviour is a command, every tool is plain Swift, and every engine is a protocol, you can test the whole agent with no language model, no network and no device. Write Swift Testing tests for the store, the toolbox and the assistant's view model.

Section 1

Describe a Task

Create a new iOS App project named WorkspaceAssistant in Xcode 27, with SwiftUI and iOS 26 as the deployment target. Set Swift Language Version to Swift 6 and Strict Concurrency Checking to Complete. Add the folders Domain/Models, Domain/Store and Domain/Services.

Every model is a value type that is Hashable, Codable and Sendable, so it can cross actors, be compared and be saved.

  1. Step 1

    Create TaskPriority.swift. Priority is an enum rather than a Bool, so more levels can be added later without changing every call site.

    Add TaskStatus, TaskOrigin, BoardLayout, AccentTheme and ListDensity the same way: each is a short String enum. Copy them from the Domain/Models folder of the project download.

    TaskPriority.swift
    1/// How important a task is. An enum rather than a `Bool` so more levels can be added later.2public enum TaskPriority: String, CaseIterable, Codable, Sendable {3    case normal, high4}

  2. Step 2

    Create TaskCategory.swift. Each category supplies a default colour and SF Symbol, so a task only stores an appearance when the user customises it. Copy TileColor.swift, the twelve tile colours, from the download.

    TaskCategory.swift
    1/// The kind of work a task represents. Each category has a default tile appearance.2public enum TaskCategory: String, CaseIterable, Codable, Sendable, Identifiable {3    case development, testing, design, operations4 5    public var id: String { rawValue }6 7    /// Default colour and glyph for tiles in this category (overridable per task).8    public var defaultAppearance: TileAppearance {9        switch self {10        case .development: TileAppearance(color: .blue, glyph: "hammer.fill")11        case .testing: TileAppearance(color: .green, glyph: "checkmark.seal.fill")12        case .design: TileAppearance(color: .pink, glyph: "paintbrush.pointed.fill")13        case .operations: TileAppearance(color: .orange, glyph: "gearshape.2.fill")14        }15    }16}

  3. Step 3

    Create TileAppearance.swift: a colour and a glyph, like a Shortcut's icon.

    TileAppearance.swift
    1/// A tile's colour and SF Symbol glyph, like a Shortcut's icon.2public struct TileAppearance: Hashable, Codable, Sendable {3    /// Tile background colour.4    public var color: TileColor5    /// SF Symbol name drawn on the tile.6    public var glyph: String7 8    public init(color: TileColor, glyph: String) {9        self.color = color10        self.glyph = glyph11    }12}

  4. Step 4

    Create TaskStep.swift for a task's optional checklist.

    TaskStep.swift
    1import Foundation2 3/// One item in a task's optional checklist.4public struct TaskStep: Identifiable, Hashable, Codable, Sendable {5    public let id: UUID6    public var title: String7    public var isDone: Bool8 9    public init(id: UUID = UUID(), title: String, isDone: Bool = false) {10        self.id = id11        self.title = title12        self.isDone = isDone13    }14}

  5. Step 5

    Create TaskItem.swift with the stored properties. appearance is optional (nil means "use the category default"), and sortIndex is a Double, so a task can be moved between two others by averaging their indexes without renumbering the rest.

    TaskItem.swift

  6. Step 6

    Add computed helpers. Views and tools ask questions like isDone and stepProgress instead of repeating the logic.

    TaskItem.swift

  7. Step 7

    Create SampleData.swift: the six tasks every new install starts with.

    SampleData.swift
    1import Foundation2 3/// The six tasks seeded on first launch (carried over from the prototype).4public enum SampleData {5    /// Fresh copies of the sample tasks, ordered by `sortIndex`.6    public static func tasks(now: Date = .now) -> [TaskItem] {7        let specs: [(String, TaskCategory, [String])] = [8            ("Refactor Network Layer", .development, ["Audit URLSession call sites", "Introduce async API client", "Migrate feed endpoints"]),9            ("Write Unit Test Suite", .testing, ["Cover the command layer", "Add persistence round-trip tests"]),10            ("Redesign Onboarding Flow", .design, []),11            ("Set Up CI/CD Pipeline", .operations, ["Configure build workflow", "Add TestFlight upload"]),12            ("Fix Memory Leak in Feed", .development, []),13            ("Accessibility Audit", .testing, ["VoiceOver pass", "Dynamic Type at AX5"]),14        ]15        return specs.enumerated().map { index, spec in16            TaskItem(17                title: spec.0,18                category: spec.1,19                steps: spec.2.map { TaskStep(title: $0) },20                createdAt: now.addingTimeInterval(Double(-index) * 3600),21                sortIndex: Double(index)22            )23        }24    }25}

Section 2

Describe Every Change as a Command

This is the idea the whole app is built on: every change goes through one place, as a command. A tap on ★ and an assistant tool both produce the same WorkspaceCommand. That gives you undo for everything, an assistant that can never do more than the user, and behaviour you can test one command at a time.

  1. Step 1

    Create WorkspaceCommand.swift. Read the cases as the app's full list of capabilities. A few exist mainly to undo others: insertTasks reverses a delete, and replaceTasks restores snapshots after an edit.

    WorkspaceCommand.swift
    1import Foundation2 3/// Every mutation of workspace state, whether issued by the user or by the assistant.4///5/// Adding a capability means adding a case here, a handler in `WorkspaceStore`, and optionally a tool.6public enum WorkspaceCommand: Hashable, Sendable {7    case addTask(title: String, category: TaskCategory, priority: TaskPriority, origin: TaskOrigin)8    /// Inserts fully-formed tasks (new-task sheet, undo of delete). Existing ids are replaced.9    case insertTasks([TaskItem])10    case updateTask(id: UUID, changes: TaskChanges)11    case setPriority(ids: [UUID], TaskPriority)12    case setStatus(ids: [UUID], TaskStatus)13    case deleteTasks(ids: [UUID])14    /// Moves a task so it ends up at `toIndex` in the full ordered task list.15    case moveTask(id: UUID, toIndex: Int)16    case setAppearance(id: UUID, TileAppearance?)17    /// Duplicates a task directly after the original, using `title` for the copy.18    case duplicateTask(id: UUID, title: String)19    case addStep(taskID: UUID, title: String)20    case toggleStep(taskID: UUID, stepID: UUID)21    case renameStep(taskID: UUID, stepID: UUID, title: String)22    case deleteStep(taskID: UUID, stepID: UUID)23    case moveSteps(taskID: UUID, fromOffsets: IndexSet, toOffset: Int)24    /// Restores task snapshots wholesale. Used as the inverse of field-level edits.25    case replaceTasks([TaskItem])26    case setLayout(BoardLayout)27    case setAccent(AccentTheme)28    case setListDensity(ListDensity)29}

  2. Step 2

    Create TaskChanges.swift, a partial update where nil means "leave this field alone".

    TaskChanges.swift
    1/// A partial update to a task's editable fields. `nil` means "leave unchanged".2public struct TaskChanges: Hashable, Sendable {3    public var title: String?4    public var notes: String?5    public var category: TaskCategory?6    public var priority: TaskPriority?7    public var status: TaskStatus?8 9    public init(10        title: String? = nil,11        notes: String? = nil,12        category: TaskCategory? = nil,13        priority: TaskPriority? = nil,14        status: TaskStatus? = nil15    ) {16        self.title = title17        self.notes = notes18        self.category = category19        self.priority = priority20        self.status = status21    }22 23    /// Whether the change set contains no edits.24    public var isEmpty: Bool {25        title == nil && notes == nil && category == nil && priority == nil && status == nil26    }27}

  3. Step 3

    Create CommandResult.swift. It separates the tasks a command targeted from the tasks that actually changed. The assistant needs that difference to report "already high priority, nothing changed" truthfully.

    CommandResult.swift
    1import Foundation2 3/// The factual outcome of performing a command.4public struct CommandResult: Hashable, Sendable {5    /// Tasks the command targeted (whether or not their values changed).6    public var affectedTaskIDs: [UUID]7    /// Tasks whose stored values actually changed.8    public var changedTaskIDs: [UUID]9    /// The task created by `addTask` or `duplicateTask`, if any.10    public var createdTaskID: UUID?11    /// The step created by `addStep`, if any.12    public var createdStepID: UUID?13 14    public init(15        affectedTaskIDs: [UUID] = [],16        changedTaskIDs: [UUID] = [],17        createdTaskID: UUID? = nil,18        createdStepID: UUID? = nil19    ) {20        self.affectedTaskIDs = affectedTaskIDs21        self.changedTaskIDs = changedTaskIDs22        self.createdTaskID = createdTaskID23        self.createdStepID = createdStepID24    }25 26    /// Whether anything actually changed.27    public var didChange: Bool { !changedTaskIDs.isEmpty }28}

  4. Step 4

    Create WorkspaceError.swift for commands the store rejects. Then copy the remaining model files from the download: CommandActor, WorkspacePreferences, ActivityEntry, AssistantChange and TaskMatch. You'll meet each of them in the next tutorial.

    WorkspaceError.swift
    1import Foundation2 3/// Reasons a command can be rejected.4public enum WorkspaceError: Error, Hashable, Sendable {5    case taskNotFound(UUID)6    case stepNotFound(UUID)7    case emptyTitle8}

Tutorial 2 of 8 · 35 min

The Store and Undo

Build WorkspaceStore, the single source of truth. It applies commands, keeps tasks in order, saves through a protocol, records who changed what, and registers an undo for every change, including the assistant's.

Download Project Files

Section 1

Define the Store's Boundaries

The store depends on small protocols instead of concrete storage. The app plugs in SwiftData and UserDefaults; tests and previews plug in memory. The assistant's tools depend on a protocol too, so they never see the store's internals.

  1. Step 1

    In Domain/Store, create WorkspaceCommandExecutor.swift: everything a tool is allowed to do. Read tasks and preferences, perform a command, and resolve words to tasks. Nothing else.

    WorkspaceCommandExecutor.swift
    1import Foundation2 3/// The surface tools and features use to read and mutate the workspace.4/// `WorkspaceStore` is the production implementation.5@MainActor6public protocol WorkspaceCommandExecutor: AnyObject, Sendable {7    /// All tasks in display order.8    var tasks: [TaskItem] { get }9    /// Current presentation preferences.10    var preferences: WorkspacePreferences { get }11    /// Performs a command, registering undo and persisting the result.12    @discardableResult13    func perform(_ command: WorkspaceCommand, actor: CommandActor) throws -> CommandResult14    /// Resolves a free-text query to tasks.15    func resolveTasks(matching query: String) -> TaskMatch16}

  2. Step 2

    Create TaskRepository.swift: load, upsert and delete. The store never says "SwiftData".

    TaskRepository.swift
    1import Foundation2 3/// Durable storage for tasks. Implemented with SwiftData in `Domain/Services/Persistence/`4/// and in memory for previews and tests.5@MainActor6public protocol TaskRepository: AnyObject {7    /// Loads every stored task (any order).8    func fetchAll() throws -> [TaskItem]9    /// Inserts or updates the given tasks by id.10    func upsert(_ tasks: [TaskItem]) throws11    /// Deletes tasks with the given ids. Unknown ids are ignored.12    func delete(ids: [UUID]) throws13}

  3. Step 3

    Create PreferencesStore.swift for the layout, accent colour and list density, plus a flag that remembers whether the sample tasks were already added.

    PreferencesStore.swift
    1/// Storage for `WorkspacePreferences` and first-launch bookkeeping.2@MainActor3public protocol PreferencesStore: AnyObject {4    /// Loads saved preferences, or defaults.5    func load() -> WorkspacePreferences6    /// Saves preferences.7    func save(_ preferences: WorkspacePreferences)8    /// Whether the sample tasks have already been seeded once.9    var hasSeededSampleTasks: Bool { get set }10}

  4. Step 4

    Create InMemoryTaskRepository.swift. Copy InMemoryPreferencesStore.swift, Log.swift (shared Logger categories) and Array+Move.swift (reordering for checklist steps) from the download.

    InMemoryTaskRepository.swift
    1import Foundation2 3/// A `TaskRepository` that keeps tasks in memory. For previews and tests.4@MainActor5public final class InMemoryTaskRepository: TaskRepository {6    private var storage: [UUID: TaskItem]7 8    public init(tasks: [TaskItem] = []) {9        storage = Dictionary(uniqueKeysWithValues: tasks.map { ($0.id, $0) })10    }11 12    public func fetchAll() throws -> [TaskItem] { Array(storage.values) }13 14    public func upsert(_ tasks: [TaskItem]) throws {15        for task in tasks { storage[task.id] = task }16    }17 18    public func delete(ids: [UUID]) throws {19        for id in ids { storage[id] = nil }20    }21}

Section 2

Build the Store

WorkspaceStore is @MainActor and @Observable, so SwiftUI redraws whenever tasks or preferences change. Its properties are private(set): the only way to change them is perform(_:actor:).

  1. Step 1

    Create TaskMatcher.swift. It turns words such as "the network refactor" into "Refactor Network Layer": by id, then exact title, then phrase, then every meaningful word. When several tasks match, it says so rather than guessing.

    TaskMatcher.swift
    1import Foundation2 3/// Resolves free-text queries ("the network refactor") to tasks.4///5/// Matching is case-, diacritic- and width-insensitive. It tries, in order: an id, an exact title,6/// a title containing the phrase, then titles containing every meaningful word (prefix match, so7/// "testing" matches "Test"). Open tasks are searched first; done tasks only if nothing open matches.8public enum TaskMatcher {9    /// Words ignored when matching word-by-word.10    static let stopWords: Set<String> = [11        "a", "an", "the", "my", "our", "this", "that", "task", "tasks", "item", "to", "for", "of", "on", "in", "and",12    ]13 14    /// Resolves `query` against `tasks`.15    public static func match(_ query: String, in tasks: [TaskItem]) -> TaskMatch {16        let trimmed = query.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)17        if let id = UUID(uuidString: trimmed), let task = tasks.first(where: { $0.id == id }) {18            return .unique(task)19        }20        let open = tasks.filter { !$0.isDone }21        let firstPass = match(normalized: normalize(trimmed), in: open)22        if firstPass != .none { return firstPass }23        return match(normalized: normalize(trimmed), in: tasks.filter(\.isDone))24    }25 26    /// Folds case, diacritics and width, strips punctuation, and collapses whitespace.27    public static func normalize(_ text: String) -> String {28        let folded = text.folding(options: [.caseInsensitive, .diacriticInsensitive, .widthInsensitive], locale: nil)29        let cleaned = folded.unicodeScalars.map { CharacterSet.alphanumerics.contains($0) ? Character($0) : " " }30        return String(cleaned).split(whereSeparator: \.isWhitespace).joined(separator: " ")31    }32 33    private static func match(normalized query: String, in tasks: [TaskItem]) -> TaskMatch {34        guard !query.isEmpty, !tasks.isEmpty else { return .none }35        let titled = tasks.map { (task: $0, title: normalize($0.title)) }36 37        let exact = titled.filter { $0.title == query }.map(\.task)38        if let result = resolve(exact) { return result }39 40        let phrase = titled.filter { $0.title.contains(query) }.map(\.task)41        if let result = resolve(phrase) { return result }42 43        let tokens = query.split(separator: " ").map(String.init).filter { !stopWords.contains($0) }44        guard !tokens.isEmpty else { return .none }45        let candidates = titled.filter { entry in46            let words = entry.title.split(separator: " ").map(String.init)47            return tokens.allSatisfy { token in words.contains { Self.matchesWord(token: token, word: $0) } }48        }.map(\.task)49        return resolve(candidates) ?? .none50    }51 52    private static func matchesWord(token: String, word: String) -> Bool {53        if word.hasPrefix(token) { return true }54        // Allow simple inflections: "testing" → "test", "refactoring" → "refactor".55        return word.count >= 4 && token.hasPrefix(word)56    }57 58    private static func resolve(_ candidates: [TaskItem]) -> TaskMatch? {59        switch candidates.count {60        case 0: nil61        case 1: .unique(candidates[0])62        default: .ambiguous(candidates)63        }64    }65}

  2. Step 2

    Create WorkspaceStore.swift with its state and initializer. On the very first launch it adds the sample tasks, and it remembers that it did, so deleting every task later doesn't bring them back.

    WorkspaceStore.swift
    1import Foundation2import Observation3import os4 5/// The single source of truth the UI observes. Every mutation goes through `perform(_:actor:)`.6@MainActor7@Observable8public final class WorkspaceStore {9    /// All tasks, sorted by `sortIndex`.10    public private(set) var tasks: [TaskItem] = []11    /// Presentation preferences.12    public private(set) var preferences: WorkspacePreferences13 14    @ObservationIgnored private let repository: any TaskRepository15    @ObservationIgnored private let preferencesStore: any PreferencesStore16 17    /// Loads tasks and preferences, seeding the sample tasks on first launch only.18    public init(19        repository: any TaskRepository,20        preferencesStore: any PreferencesStore,21        seed: @autoclosure () -> [TaskItem] = SampleData.tasks()22    ) {23        self.repository = repository24        self.preferencesStore = preferencesStore25        preferences = preferencesStore.load()26 27        var loaded: [TaskItem] = []28        do {29            loaded = try repository.fetchAll()30        } catch {31            Log.persistence.error("Failed to load tasks: \(error.localizedDescription, privacy: .public)")32        }33        if loaded.isEmpty && !preferencesStore.hasSeededSampleTasks {34            loaded = seed()35            do {36                try repository.upsert(loaded)37            } catch {38                Log.persistence.error("Failed to seed tasks: \(error.localizedDescription, privacy: .public)")39            }40        }41        preferencesStore.hasSeededSampleTasks = true42        tasks = loaded.sorted(by: Self.ordering)43    }44 45    /// Returns the task with the given id, if it exists.46    public func task(id: UUID) -> TaskItem? {47        tasks.first { $0.id == id }48    }49 50    public func resolveTasks(matching query: String) -> TaskMatch {51        TaskMatcher.match(query, in: tasks)52    }53 54    // MARK: - Ordering55 56    private static func ordering(_ lhs: TaskItem, _ rhs: TaskItem) -> Bool {57        lhs.sortIndex == rhs.sortIndex ? lhs.createdAt > rhs.createdAt : lhs.sortIndex < rhs.sortIndex58    }59 60    /// A sort index that places an item at `index` within `ordered` (which must be sorted).61    static func sortIndex(at index: Int, in ordered: [TaskItem]) -> Double {62        switch (ordered.indices.contains(index - 1) ? ordered[index - 1] : nil, ordered.indices.contains(index) ? ordered[index] : nil) {63        case (nil, nil): 064        case let (nil, next?): next.sortIndex - 165        case let (previous?, nil): previous.sortIndex + 166        case let (previous?, next?): (previous.sortIndex + next.sortIndex) / 267        }68    }69}

  3. Step 3

    Add perform(_:actor:) and the apply(_:) switch, and conform to WorkspaceCommandExecutor. Each case returns an Outcome: the result, the inverse command that would undo it, and which tasks to save or delete. New tasks get a sortIndex below the current minimum, so they appear at the top.

{56        let previousPreferences = preferences57        let outcome = try apply(command)58        tasks.sort(by: Self.ordering)59        persist(outcome, preferencesChanged: previousPreferences != Applying commands65 66    /// What applying a command did, and how to reverse it.67    private struct Outcome {68        var result = CommandResult()69        var inverse: WorkspaceCommand?70        var upserted: [UUID] = []71        var deleted: [UUID] = []72    }73 74    private func apply(_ command: WorkspaceCommand) throws -> Outcome {75        switch command {76        case let Section 3

Record Activity and Undo Everything

Because each command already knows its inverse, undo is one small function. The store registers the inverse with the scene's UndoManager; undoing performs it, which registers the redo. Shake to undo, or press ⌘Z, and it works for the assistant's changes too.

  1. Step 1

Tutorial 3 of 8 · 20 min

Saving with SwiftData

Implement the store's storage protocols. Tasks are saved with SwiftData through a storage model that mirrors TaskItem; preferences go to UserDefaults. Then create the composition root that decides which implementations the app uses.

Download Project Files

Section 1

Map Tasks to SwiftData

Keep TaskItem a plain struct and add a separate @Model class for storage. The domain never depends on SwiftData, and the storage format can change without touching the rest of the app.

In Domain/Services, add a Persistence folder.

  1. Step 1

    Create TaskRecord.swift. Every property has a default and there are no unique constraints, so the schema could later sync through CloudKit. Enums are stored as raw strings and steps as JSON. update(from:) copies every field from a TaskItem.

    TaskRecord.swift
    1import Foundation2import SwiftData3 4/// SwiftData storage model for a `TaskItem`.5///6/// Every property has a default and there are no unique constraints, so the schema can later sync7/// through CloudKit. Enums are stored as raw strings and steps as JSON so the domain stays decoupled.8@Model9final class TaskRecord {10    var id: UUID = UUID()11    var title: String = ""12    var notes: String = ""13    var categoryRaw: String = TaskCategory.development.rawValue14    var priorityRaw: String = TaskPriority.normal.rawValue15    var statusRaw: String = TaskStatus.open.rawValue16    var originRaw: String = TaskOrigin.user.rawValue17    var appearanceColorRaw: String?18    var appearanceGlyph: String?19    var stepsData: Data = Data()20    var createdAt: Date = Date.now21    var sortIndex: Double = 022 23    init(task: TaskItem) {24        id = task.id25        update(from: task)26    }27 28    /// Copies every field from a domain task.29    func update(from task: TaskItem) {30        title = task.title31        notes = task.notes32        categoryRaw = task.category.rawValue33        priorityRaw = task.priority.rawValue34        statusRaw = task.status.rawValue35        originRaw = task.origin.rawValue36        appearanceColorRaw = task.appearance?.color.rawValue37        appearanceGlyph = task.appearance?.glyph38        stepsData = (try? JSONEncoder().encode(task.steps)) ?? Data()39        createdAt = task.createdAt40        sortIndex = task.sortIndex41    }42}

  2. Step 2

    Add taskItem, the conversion back. Unknown raw values fall back to defaults, so a value written by a newer version of the app can't crash this one.

Section 2

Implement the Repository

SwiftDataTaskRepository owns a ModelContainer and works on its main context, which matches the store's @MainActor isolation.

  1. Step 1

    Create SwiftDataTaskRepository.swift with the container and fetchAll(). Passing inMemory: true gives tests a throwaway store with the same code path.

    SwiftDataTaskRepository.swift
    1import Foundation2import SwiftData3 4/// A `TaskRepository` backed by SwiftData.5@MainActor6public final class SwiftDataTaskRepository: TaskRepository {7    private let container: ModelContainer8    private var context: ModelContext { container.mainContext }9 10    /// Creates a repository. Pass `inMemory: true` for tests.11    public init(inMemory: Bool = false) throws {12        let configuration = ModelConfiguration(isStoredInMemoryOnly: inMemory)13        container = try ModelContainer(for: TaskRecord.self, configurations: configuration)14    }15 16    public func fetchAll() throws -> [TaskItem] {17        try context.fetch(FetchDescriptor<TaskRecord>(sortBy: [SortDescriptor(\.sortIndex)])).map(\.taskItem)18    }19}

  2. Step 2

    Add upsert(_:). It fetches the existing records for the given ids with one #Predicate, updates those it finds and inserts the rest, then saves once.

    SwiftDataTaskRepository.swift
    ⋯1import Foundation2import SwiftData3 4/// A `TaskRepository` backed by SwiftData.5@MainActor6public final class SwiftDataTaskRepository: TaskRepository {7    private let container: ModelContainer8    private var context: ModelContext { container.mainContext }9 10    /// Creates a repository. Pass `inMemory: true` for tests.11    public init(inMemory: Bool = false) throws {12        let configuration = ModelConfiguration(isStoredInMemoryOnly: inMemory)13        container = try ModelContainer(for: TaskRecord.self, configurations: configuration)14    }15 16    public func fetchAll() throws -> [TaskItem] {17        try context.fetch(FetchDescriptor<TaskRecord>(sortBy: [SortDescriptor(\.sortIndex)])).map(\.taskItem)18    }19 20    public func upsert(_ tasks: [TaskItem]) throws {21        guard !tasks.isEmpty else { return }22        let ids = tasks.map(\.id)23        let existing = try context.fetch(FetchDescriptor<TaskRecord>(predicate: #Predicate { ids.contains($0.id) }))24        let byID = Dictionary(existing.map { ($0.id, $0) }, uniquingKeysWith: { first, _ in first })25        for task in tasks {26            if let record = byID[task.id] {27                record.update(from: task)28            } else {29                context.insert(TaskRecord(task: task))30            }31        }32        try context.save()33    }34}

  3. Step 3

    Add delete(ids:), a batch delete with a predicate.

    SwiftDataTaskRepository.swift
    ⋯1import Foundation2import SwiftData3 4/// A `TaskRepository` backed by SwiftData.5@MainActor6public final class SwiftDataTaskRepository: TaskRepository {7    private let container: ModelContainer8    private var context: ModelContext { container.mainContext }9 10    /// Creates a repository. Pass `inMemory: true` for tests.11    public init(inMemory: Bool = false) throws {12        let configuration = ModelConfiguration(isStoredInMemoryOnly: inMemory)13        container = try ModelContainer(for: TaskRecord.self, configurations: configuration)14    }15 16    public func fetchAll() throws -> [TaskItem] {17        try context.fetch(FetchDescriptor<TaskRecord>(sortBy: [SortDescriptor(\.sortIndex)])).map(\.taskItem)18    }19 20    public func upsert(_ tasks: [TaskItem]) throws {21        guard !tasks.isEmpty else { return }22        let ids = tasks.map(\.id)23        let existing = try context.fetch(FetchDescriptor<TaskRecord>(predicate: #Predicate { ids.contains($0.id) }))24        let byID = Dictionary(existing.map { ($0.id, $0) }, uniquingKeysWith: { first, _ in first })25        for task in tasks {26            if let record = byID[task.id] {27                record.update(from: task)28            } else {29                context.insert(TaskRecord(task: task))30            }31        }32        try context.save()33    }34 35    public func delete(ids: [UUID]) throws {36        guard !ids.isEmpty else { return }37        try context.delete(model: TaskRecord.self, where: #Predicate { ids.contains($0.id) })38        try context.save()39    }40}

Section 3

Preferences and the Composition Root

One object decides which implementations to use, once per launch. Everything else receives its dependencies instead of creating them.

  1. Step 1

    Create UserDefaultsPreferencesStore.swift, the same storage @AppStorage uses.

    UserDefaultsPreferencesStore.swift
    1import Foundation2 3/// A `PreferencesStore` backed by `UserDefaults` (the same storage `@AppStorage` uses).4@MainActor5public final class UserDefaultsPreferencesStore: PreferencesStore {6    private enum Key {7        static let layout = "preferences.layout"8        static let accent = "preferences.accent"9        static let listDensity = "preferences.listDensity"10        static let seeded = "preferences.hasSeededSampleTasks"11    }12 13    private let defaults: UserDefaults14 15    public init(defaults: UserDefaults = .standard) {16        self.defaults = defaults17    }18 19    public func load() -> WorkspacePreferences {20        let fallback = WorkspacePreferences()21        return WorkspacePreferences(22            layout: defaults.string(forKey: Key.layout).flatMap(BoardLayout.init(rawValue:)) ?? fallback.layout,23            accent: defaults.string(forKey: Key.accent).flatMap(AccentTheme.init(rawValue:)) ?? fallback.accent,24            listDensity: defaults.string(forKey: Key.listDensity).flatMap(ListDensity.init(rawValue:)) ?? fallback.listDensity25        )26    }27 28    public func save(_ preferences: WorkspacePreferences) {29        defaults.set(preferences.layout.rawValue, forKey: Key.layout)30        defaults.set(preferences.accent.rawValue, forKey: Key.accent)31        defaults.set(preferences.listDensity.rawValue, forKey: Key.listDensity)32    }33 34    public var hasSeededSampleTasks: Bool {35        get { defaults.bool(forKey: Key.seeded) }36        set { defaults.set(newValue, forKey: Key.seeded) }37    }38}

  2. Step 2

    At the top level of the app folder, create LaunchConfiguration.swift. Launch arguments such as -UITestScriptedAssistant switch to in-memory storage and the scripted assistant, so UI tests are repeatable. The switches only work in debug builds.

    LaunchConfiguration.swift
    1import Foundation2 3/// Behaviour switches read from launch arguments (used by UI tests and design review).4/// They only take effect in DEBUG builds; release builds always use real storage and the app UI.5struct LaunchConfiguration {6    /// `-UITestScriptedAssistant`: in-memory storage and the scripted assistant.7    let isUITest: Bool8    /// `-DesignGallery`: show the design-system gallery instead of the app.9    let showsDesignGallery: Bool10 11    /// Set when the app is hosting the unit test bundle; it then avoids the on-disk store.12    let isUnitTestHost: Bool13 14    init(arguments: [String] = ProcessInfo.processInfo.arguments, environment: [String: String] = ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment) {15        #if DEBUG16        isUnitTestHost = environment["XCTestConfigurationFilePath"] != nil17        isUITest = arguments.contains("-UITestScriptedAssistant")18        showsDesignGallery = arguments.contains("-DesignGallery")19        #else20        isUnitTestHost = false21        isUITest = false22        showsDesignGallery = false23        #endif24    }25 26    /// Whether to avoid touching persistent storage.27    var usesEphemeralStorage: Bool { isUITest || isUnitTestHost }28}

  3. Step 3

    Create AppDependencies.swift. It picks SwiftData or memory, falls back to memory if the SwiftData store can't open, and builds the store. You'll add the view models and the assistant here in later tutorials.

    AppDependencies.swift
    1import Foundation2import os3 4/// Composition root: builds storage, the store and feature models once per launch.5@MainActor6final class AppDependencies {7    let store: WorkspaceStore8    let launch: LaunchConfiguration9 10    init(launch: LaunchConfiguration = LaunchConfiguration()) {11        self.launch = launch12        let repository: any TaskRepository13        let preferences: any PreferencesStore14        if launch.usesEphemeralStorage {15            repository = InMemoryTaskRepository()16            preferences = InMemoryPreferencesStore()17        } else {18            do {19                repository = try SwiftDataTaskRepository()20            } catch {21                Log.persistence.fault("Falling back to in-memory storage: \(error.localizedDescription, privacy: .public)")22                repository = InMemoryTaskRepository()23            }24            preferences = UserDefaultsPreferencesStore()25        }26        store = WorkspaceStore(repository: repository, preferencesStore: preferences)27    }28}

Section 1

Build the Board's View Model

BoardViewModel holds screen state (selection, sort order, which sheet is showing) and offers actions such as togglePriority. Every action ends in store.perform(_:actor: .user), exactly where the assistant's tools will end.

  1. Step 1

    Copy the ViewModels/Board folder from the download. These small types describe the board: collections, sort orders, the three Board columns, and requests such as "reveal this task". BoardCollection is a good example: one enum gives each collection its title, symbol, colour and filter.

    BoardCollection.swift
    1import Foundation2 3/// A filtered view of the workspace: all tasks, priority, done, or a category.4public enum BoardCollection: Hashable, Sendable, Identifiable {5    case all6    case priority7    case done8    case category(TaskCategory)9 10    public var id: String {11        switch self {12        case .all: "all"13        case .priority: "priority"14        case .done: "done"15        case let .category(category): "category.\(category.rawValue)"16        }17    }18 19    /// Every collection, in sidebar order.20    public static var allCases: [BoardCollection] {21        [.all, .priority, .done] + TaskCategory.allCases.map(BoardCollection.category)22    }23 24    /// Localised title.25    public var title: String {26        switch self {27        case .all: String(localized: "Tasks")28        case .priority: String(localized: "Priority")29        case .done: String(localized: "Done")30        case let .category(category): category.displayName31        }32    }33 34    /// SF Symbol for the collection.35    public var symbolName: String {36        switch self {37        case .all: "square.grid.2x2.fill"38        case .priority: "star.fill"39        case .done: "checkmark.circle.fill"40        case let .category(category): category.symbolName41        }42    }43 44    /// Tile colour for the collection's glyph square.45    public var color: TileColor {46        switch self {47        case .all: .indigo48        case .priority: .orange49        case .done: .gray50        case let .category(category): category.defaultAppearance.color51        }52    }53 54    /// The category new tasks should default to when created from this collection.55    public var defaultCategory: TaskCategory {56        if case let .category(category) = self { return category }57        return .development58    }59 60    /// Whether a task belongs to this collection, ignoring done/open state.61    func contains(_ task: TaskItem) -> Bool {62        switch self {63        case .all, .done: true64        case .priority: task.isHighPriority65        case let .category(category): task.category == category66        }67    }68 69    /// Tasks shown for this collection in a layout. Only the Board layout and the Done collection show done tasks.70    func visibleTasks(_ tasks: [TaskItem], layout: BoardLayout) -> [TaskItem] {71        tasks.filter { task in72            guard contains(task) else { return false }73            switch self {74            case .done: return task.isDone75            default: return layout == .board || !task.isDone76            }77        }78    }79}

  2. Step 2

    Create ViewModels/BoardViewModel.swift with its state, queries and single-task actions. highlightTrigger(for:) returns the id of the assistant's latest change when it touched this task; the tile will pulse when that id changes. perform(_:) logs failures instead of crashing.

    BoardViewModel.swift
    1import Foundation2import Observation3import os4 5/// State and actions for the board: selection, sorting, presentations, and user-issued commands.6///7/// Every mutation is forwarded to `WorkspaceStore` as a `WorkspaceCommand` with `actor: .user`.8@MainActor9@Observable10public final class BoardViewModel {11    /// The shared store.12    public let store: WorkspaceStore13 14    /// Whether multi-select mode is on. Turning it off clears the selection.15    public var isSelecting = false {16        didSet { if !isSelecting { selection.removeAll() } }17    }18    /// Selected task ids in multi-select mode.19    public var selection: Set<UUID> = []20    /// Current ordering. Persisted when the model was created with `sortStorage`.21    public var sort: BoardSort = .manual {22        didSet { sortStorage?.set(sort.rawValue, forKey: Self.sortKey) }23    }24    /// Task whose appearance picker is showing.25    public var appearanceTaskID: UUID?26    /// Deletion awaiting confirmation.27    public var pendingDeletion: PendingDeletion?28    /// Presents the new-task sheet when set.29    public var newTask: NewTaskRequest?30    /// Presents the settings sheet.31    public var isShowingSettings = false32    /// Asks the visible layout to scroll to a task.33    public private(set) var revealRequest: RevealRequest?34    /// Set when a detail view should close because its task was deleted.35    public private(set) var deletedTaskIDs: Set<UUID> = []36 37    @ObservationIgnored private let sortStorage: UserDefaults?38    private static let sortKey = "board.sort"39 40    /// - Parameter sortStorage: Where to remember the sort order across launches (`nil` = don't persist).41    public init(store: WorkspaceStore, sortStorage: UserDefaults? = nil) {42        self.store = store43        self.sortStorage = sortStorage44        if let raw = sortStorage?.string(forKey: Self.sortKey), let saved = BoardSort(rawValue: raw) {45            sort = saved46        }47    }48 49    // MARK: - Queries50 51    /// Tasks for a collection in the current layout and sort order.52    public func tasks(in collection: BoardCollection) -> [TaskItem] {53        sort.sorted(collection.visibleTasks(store.tasks, layout: store.preferences.layout))54    }55 56    /// Number of open tasks (or done tasks, for the Done collection) in a collection, for badges.57    public func count(in collection: BoardCollection) -> Int {58        collection.visibleTasks(store.tasks, layout: .grid).count59    }60 61    /// Whether drag-to-reorder is available.62    public var canReorder: Bool { sort == .manual && !isSelecting }63 64    /// The pulse trigger for a task, if the assistant just changed it.65    public func highlightTrigger(for id: UUID) -> UUID? {66        guard let change = store.lastAssistantChange, change.taskIDs.contains(id) else { return nil }67        return change.id68    }69 70    // MARK: - Single-task actions71 72    /// Toggles high priority.73    public func togglePriority(_ id: UUID) {74        guard let task = store.task(id: id) else { return }75        perform(.setPriority(ids: [id], task.isHighPriority ? .normal : .high))76    }77 78    /// Toggles done/open.79    public func toggleDone(_ id: UUID) {80        guard let task = store.task(id: id) else { return }81        perform(.setStatus(ids: [id], task.isDone ? .open : .done))82    }83 84    /// Duplicates a task next to the original.85    public func duplicate(_ id: UUID) {86        guard let task = store.task(id: id) else { return }87        perform(.duplicateTask(id: id, title: String(localized: "\(task.title) Copy")))88    }89 90    /// Deletes immediately (undoable).91    public func delete(_ ids: [UUID]) {92        guard !ids.isEmpty else { return }93        perform(.deleteTasks(ids: ids))94        deletedTaskIDs.formUnion(ids)95        selection.subtract(ids)96    }97 98    /// Asks for confirmation before deleting.99    public func requestDelete(_ ids: [UUID]) {100        guard !ids.isEmpty else { return }101        pendingDeletion = PendingDeletion(taskIDs: ids)102    }103 104    /// Performs the pending deletion.105    public func confirmPendingDeletion() {106        guard let pending = pendingDeletion else { return }107        pendingDeletion = nil108        delete(pending.taskIDs)109        isSelecting = false110    }111 112    /// Moves tasks to a category.113    public func move(_ ids: [UUID], to category: TaskCategory) {114        let undo = store.undoManager115        undo?.beginUndoGrouping()116        for id in ids { perform(.updateTask(id: id, changes: TaskChanges(category: category))) }117        undo?.endUndoGrouping()118    }119 120    /// Sets the board layout.121    public func setLayout(_ layout: BoardLayout) {122        perform(.setLayout(layout))123    }124 125    /// Scrolls the visible layout to a task.126    public func reveal(_ id: UUID) {127        revealRequest = RevealRequest(taskID: id)128    }129 130    /// Presents the new-task sheet.131    public func createTask(in collection: BoardCollection = .all) {132        newTask = NewTaskRequest(category: collection.defaultCategory)133    }134 135    // MARK: - Commands136 137    /// Performs a user command, logging failures.138    @discardableResult139    public func perform(_ command: WorkspaceCommand) -> CommandResult? {140        do {141            return try store.perform(command, actor: .user)142        } catch {143            Log.ui.error("Command failed: \(String(describing: error), privacy: .public)")144            return nil145        }146    }147}

  3. Step 3

    Add multi-select. Prioritise and Complete act as toggles: if every selected task is already high priority, the same button removes priority.

  4. Step 4

    Add reordering. Drag-and-drop and List.onMove are translated into moveTask commands, so moving a tile is undoable like everything else. Dropping a task on a Board column becomes an updateTask with that column's changes.

moving = visible[from]175        if toOffset > from, visible.indices.contains(toOffset - 1) {176            place(moving.id, after: visible[toOffset - 1].id)177        } else if toIndex: index))200    }201 202    private func place(_ id: UUID, after targetID: UUID) {203        let others = store.tasks.filter { $0.id != id }204        guard let index = others.firstIndex(where: { $0.id == targetID }) else { return }205        perform(.moveTask(id: id, toIndex: index + 1))206    }207 208    // MARK: - Commands209 210    /// Performs a user command, logging failures.⋯211 Section 2

Add the Design System and Board Views

The app's look lives in Views/Shared: spacing and corner tokens, the tile palette (with high-contrast variants), and reusable components such as tiles, token pills and action blocks. Copy these folders from the download: Views/Shared, Views/Board, Views/TaskDetail, Views/Collections and Views/Search. Then look at the two files that matter most for the agent.

  1. Step 1

    Open Views/Shared/Components/TaskTile.swift. Each tile comes in three sizes. Find phaseAnimator(_:trigger:): when highlightTrigger changes, the tile scales up with a coloured glow and its glyph bounces. That's how the user sees what the assistant just changed. It respects Reduce Motion, Increase Contrast and Dynamic Type.

    TaskTile.swift

    Open Views/Board/BoardView.swift. It switches between the four layouts, cross-fades when the layout changes, animates whenever the task list changes, and plays a haptic when a task is completed. Opening a task zooms into its detail view.

.success : nil36            }37            .sensoryFeedback(.impact(weight: .light), trigger: model.store.tasks.count(where: \.isHighPriority))38    }39 40    @ViewBuilder private func content(_ tasks: [TaskItem]) -> some View {41        if tasks.isEmpty && layout != .board && layout != .focus {42            emptyState43        } else {44            switch layout {45            case .grid: GridLayoutView(tasks: tasks, namespace: namespace, onOpen: open)46            case .list: ListLayoutView(tasks: tasks, onOpen: open)47            case .focus: FocusLayoutView(tasks: tasks, namespace: namespace, onOpen: open)48            case .board: KanbanLayoutView(tasks: tasks, namespace: namespace, onOpen: open)49            }50        }51    }52 53    private var emptyState: some View {54        ContentUnavailableView {55            Label(emptyTitle, systemImage: collection.symbolName)56        } description: {57            Text(emptyMessage)58        } actions: {59            if collection != .done {60                Button {61                    model.createTask(in: collection)62                } label: {63                    Text("New Task")64                }65                .buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)66            }67        }68    }69 70    private var emptyTitle: String {71        switch collection {72        case .done: String(localized: "Nothing Done Yet")73        case .priority: String(localized: "No Priority Tasks")74        default: String(localized: "No Tasks")75        }76    }77 78    private var emptyMessage: String {79        switch collection {80        case .done: String(localized: "Completed tasks appear here.")81        case .priority: String(localized: "Prioritise a task to see it here.")82        default: String(localized: "Add a task, or ask the assistant to create one.")83        }84    }85 86    private func open(_ id: UUID) {87        path.append(TaskRoute(taskID: id))88    }89}

Section 3

Put the Board on Screen

Create the view model in the composition root and show three tabs. The root view also hands the scene's UndoManager to the store; without that line, nothing could be undone.

  1. Step 1

    In AppDependencies, create the BoardViewModel and an AppRouter for the selected tab. Copy ViewModels/AppRouter.swift and AppTab.swift from the download. undoActionName gives the Edit menu names such as "Undo Prioritise".

    AppDependencies.swift
    ⋯1import Foundation2import os3 4/// Composition root: builds storage, the store and feature models once per launch.5@MainActor6final class AppDependencies {7    let store: WorkspaceStore8    let board: BoardViewModel9    let router = AppRouter()10    let launch: LaunchConfiguration11 12    init(launch: LaunchConfiguration = LaunchConfiguration()) {⋯13        self.launch = launch14        let repository: any TaskRepository15        let preferences: any PreferencesStore16        if launch.usesEphemeralStorage {17            repository = InMemoryTaskRepository()18            preferences = InMemoryPreferencesStore()19        } else {20            do {21                repository = try SwiftDataTaskRepository()22            } catch {23                Log.persistence.fault("Falling back to in-memory storage: \(error.localizedDescription, privacy: .public)")24                repository = InMemoryTaskRepository()25            }26            preferences = UserDefaultsPreferencesStore()27        }28        store = WorkspaceStore(repository: repository, preferencesStore: preferences)29        store.undoActionName = UndoActionNames.name(for:)30        board = BoardViewModel(store: store, sortStorage: launch.usesEphemeralStorage ? nil : .standard)31    }32}

  2. Step 2

    Create Views/Root/RootView.swift with three tabs: Tasks, Collections and a Search tab with the search role. The last two lines connect the scene's undo manager to the store. The toolbar's Settings button doesn't open anything yet; its sheet arrives with the assistant.

    RootView.swift
    1import SwiftUI2 3/// The app's root: a tab bar with Tasks, Collections and Search.4struct RootView: View {5    @Environment(AppRouter.self) private var router6    @Environment(BoardViewModel.self) private var board7    @Environment(\.undoManager) private var undoManager8 9    var body: some View {10        @Bindable var router = router11        @Bindable var board = board12        TabView(selection: $router.tab) {13            Tab(value: AppTab.tasks) {14                BoardScreen(collection: .all)15            } label: {16                Label { Text("Tasks") } icon: { Image(systemName: "square.grid.2x2") }17            }18 19            Tab(value: AppTab.collections) {20                CollectionsScreen()21            } label: {22                Label { Text("Collections") } icon: { Image(systemName: "folder") }23            }24 25            Tab(value: AppTab.search, role: .search) {26                SearchScreen(query: $router.searchQuery)27            } label: {28                Label { Text("Search") } icon: { Image(systemName: "magnifyingglass") }29            }30        }31        .boardPresentations()32        .tint(board.store.preferences.accent.color)33        .onAppear { board.store.undoManager = undoManager }34        .onChange(of: undoManager) { _, manager in board.store.undoManager = manager }35    }36}

  3. Step 3

    Replace the app file. It owns AppDependencies in @State and injects the view model and router into the environment. In debug builds, the -DesignGallery launch argument shows every component instead. Run the app: tap, drag, switch layouts, then shake to undo.

    WorkspaceAssistantApp.swift
    1import SwiftUI2 3/// App entry point. Owns the composition root and injects dependencies into the environment.4@main5struct WorkspaceAssistantApp: App {6    @State private var dependencies = AppDependencies()7 8    var body: some Scene {9        WindowGroup {10            #if DEBUG11            if dependencies.launch.showsDesignGallery {12                DesignGallery()13            } else {14                root15            }16            #else17            root18            #endif19        }20    }21 22    private var root: some View {23        RootView()24            .environment(dependencies.board)25            .environment(dependencies.router)26    }27}

Up nextTools and the Toolbox

Tutorial 5 of 8 · 30 min

Tools and the Toolbox

Give the assistant hands. A toolbox resolves the model's words to tasks, performs commands as the assistant, and reports exactly what happened. Nine thin tools expose it to Foundation Models.

Download Project Files

Section 1

Describe What a Tool Did

Every tool call produces two things: a sentence for the model, and a structured activity for the UI. The sentence keeps the model honest; the activity becomes an action block in the chat and an announcement for VoiceOver.

  1. Step 1

    Create Domain/Models/ToolActivity.swift. Parameters are typed (.task, .layout, .priority…), so the UI can draw them as token pills and localise them. Outcomes are success, unchanged or a specific failure such as noMatch or ambiguous.

    ToolActivity.swift
    1import Foundation2 3/// A record of one tool call by the assistant, rendered as an action block.4public struct ToolActivity: Identifiable, Hashable, Sendable {5    public let id: UUID6    public let kind: ToolKind7    public let parameters: [ToolParameter]8    public let outcome: ToolOutcome9    /// Tasks the call referred to (for highlighting and scrolling).10    public let taskIDs: [UUID]11 12    public init(id: UUID = UUID(), kind: ToolKind, parameters: [ToolParameter], outcome: ToolOutcome, taskIDs: [UUID] = []) {13        self.id = id14        self.kind = kind15        self.parameters = parameters16        self.outcome = outcome17        self.taskIDs = taskIDs18    }19 20    /// Whether the call succeeded.21    public var succeeded: Bool {22        if case .success = outcome { return true }23        return false24    }25}26 27/// The assistant's tools.28public enum ToolKind: String, Hashable, Sendable, CaseIterable {29    case findTasks, addTask, setPriority, completeTask, deleteTask, switchLayout, setAccentColor, setTaskColor, addStep30}31 32/// A typed tool parameter, localised by the UI and drawn as a token pill.33public enum ToolParameter: Hashable, Sendable {34    case task(title: String, id: UUID?)35    case query(String)36    case text(String)37    case category(TaskCategory)38    case priority(TaskPriority)39    case layout(BoardLayout)40    case accent(AccentTheme)41    case color(TileColor)42}43 44/// What happened when a tool ran.45public enum ToolOutcome: Hashable, Sendable {46    /// The change was made (or, for lookups, results were returned).47    case success48    /// The request was valid but nothing needed to change.49    case unchanged50    /// The tool could not act.51    case failure(ToolFailure)52}53 54/// Why a tool could not act.55public enum ToolFailure: Hashable, Sendable {56    case noMatch(query: String)57    case ambiguous(query: String, candidates: [String])58    case emptyTitle59    case rejected(String)60}

  2. Step 2

    In Domain/Services/Assistant/Toolbox, create ToolResult.swift to pair the two.

    ToolResult.swift
    1 2/// The outcome of a toolbox operation: a factual message for the model and an activity for the UI.3public struct ToolResult: Hashable, Sendable {4    /// Plain-English, truthful result returned to the language model.5    public let message: String6    /// Structured record for the transcript's action block.7    public let activity: ToolActivity8}

Section 2

Build the Toolbox

The toolbox is shared by the real tools and the scripted assistant, so both behave identically. It talks to the store only through WorkspaceCommandExecutor, and always as .assistant.

  1. Step 1

    Create WorkspaceToolbox.swift with findTasks. It returns titles and ids, so the model can refer to a task precisely in a follow-up call. When nothing matches, the message lists the open tasks, so the model can recover.

    WorkspaceToolbox.swift
    1import Foundation2import os3 4/// The tools' shared logic: resolve tasks, issue `WorkspaceCommand`s as `.assistant`, and report5/// truthfully what happened — including "no match", "ambiguous" and "already done".6///7/// Used by the Foundation Models tool adapters and by `ScriptedEngine`, so both paths behave identically.8@MainActor9public final class WorkspaceToolbox: Sendable {10    private let executor: any WorkspaceCommandExecutor11 12    public init(executor: any WorkspaceCommandExecutor) {13        self.executor = executor14    }15 16    // MARK: - Lookup17 18    /// Lists tasks matching `query` (or all open tasks for an empty query) with ids and state.19    public func findTasks(query: String) -> ToolResult {20        let trimmed = query.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)21        let matches: [TaskItem]22        if trimmed.isEmpty {23            matches = executor.tasks.filter { !$0.isDone }24        } else {25            switch executor.resolveTasks(matching: trimmed) {26            case .none: matches = []27            case let .unique(task): matches = [task]28            case let .ambiguous(tasks): matches = tasks29            }30        }31        guard !matches.isEmpty else {32            return ToolResult(33                message: "No task matches '\(trimmed)'. \(openTasksSummary())",34                activity: ToolActivity(kind: .findTasks, parameters: [.query(trimmed)], outcome: .failure(.noMatch(query: trimmed)))35            )36        }37        let lines = matches.map { task in38            "- '\(task.title)' (id: \(task.id.uuidString), category: \(task.category.rawValue), priority: \(task.priority.rawValue), status: \(task.status.rawValue), steps: \(task.completedStepCount)/\(task.steps.count))"39        }40        return ToolResult(41            message: "Found \(matches.count) task(s):\n" + lines.joined(separator: "\n"),42            activity: ToolActivity(kind: .findTasks, parameters: [.query(trimmed)], outcome: .success, taskIDs: matches.map(\.id))43        )44    }45 46    // MARK: - Helpers47 48    private func openTasksSummary() -> String {49        let open = executor.tasks.filter { !$0.isDone }.map { "'\($0.title)'" }50        return open.isEmpty ? "There are no open tasks." : "Open tasks: \(open.joined(separator: ", "))."51    }52}

  2. Step 2

    Add addTask. An empty title is reported as a plain instruction to the model: "Ask the user what the task should be called."

    WorkspaceToolbox.swift
    ⋯1import Foundation2import os3 4/// The tools' shared logic: resolve tasks, issue `WorkspaceCommand`s as `.assistant`, and report5/// truthfully what happened — including "no match", "ambiguous" and "already done".6///7/// Used by the Foundation Models tool adapters and by `ScriptedEngine`, so both paths behave identically.8@MainActor9public final class WorkspaceToolbox: Sendable {10    private let executor: any WorkspaceCommandExecutor11 12    public init(executor: any WorkspaceCommandExecutor) {13        self.executor = executor14    }15 16    // MARK: - Mutations47 48    /// Creates a task.49    public func addTask(title: String, category: TaskCategory, priority: TaskPriority) -> ToolResult {50        let trimmed = title.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)51        let parameters: [ToolParameter] = [.text(trimmed), .category(category), .priority(priority)]52        do {53            let result = try executor.perform(.addTask(title: trimmed, category: category, priority: priority, origin: .assistant), actor: .assistant)54            let id = result.createdTaskID55            let priorityText = priority == .high ? "high" : "normal"56            return ToolResult(57                message: "Added '\(trimmed)' to \(category.rawValue) with \(priorityText) priority.",58                activity: ToolActivity(kind: .addTask, parameters: [.task(title: trimmed, id: id), .category(category), .priority(priority)], outcome: .success, taskIDs: id.map { [$0] } ?? [])59            )60        } catch WorkspaceError.emptyTitle {61            return ToolResult(62                message: "Not added: the title was empty. Ask the user what the task should be called.",63                activity: ToolActivity(kind: .addTask, parameters: parameters, outcome: .failure(.emptyTitle))64            )65        } catch {66            return failure(.addTask, parameters, error)67        }68    }69 70    // MARK: - Helpers71 72    private func failure(_ kind: ToolKind, _ parameters: [ToolParameter], _ error: any Error) -> ToolResult {73        Log.agent.error("Tool \(kind.rawValue, privacy: .public) failed: \(String(describing: error), privacy: .public)")74        return ToolResult(75            message: "The change failed and nothing was modified (\(String(describing: error))).",76            activity: ToolActivity(kind: kind, parameters: parameters, outcome: .failure(.rejected(String(describing: error))))77        )78    }79 80    private func openTasksSummary() -> String {81        let open = executor.tasks.filter { !$0.isDone }.map { "'\($0.title)'" }⋯82        return open.isEmpty ? "There are no open tasks." : "Open tasks: \(open.joined(separator: ", "))."83    }84}

  3. Step 3

    Add withUniqueTask, the heart of honest tools. It acts only when the words match exactly one task. For none or several it changes nothing and says so, listing the candidates. Then add priority, complete and delete on top of it. Each checks first and reports "No change made" rather than pretending.

    WorkspaceToolbox.swift
    ⋯1import Foundation2import os3 4/// The tools' shared logic: resolve tasks, issue `WorkspaceCommand`s as `.assistant`, and report5/// truthfully what happened — including "no match", "ambiguous" and "already done".6///7/// Used by the Foundation Models tool adapters and by `ScriptedEngine`, so both paths behave identically.8@MainActor9public final class WorkspaceToolbox: Sendable {10    private let executor: any WorkspaceCommandExecutor11 12    public init(executor: any WorkspaceCommandExecutor) {13        self.executor = executor14    }15 16    // MARK: - Lookup17 18    /// Lists tasks matching `query` (or all open tasks for an empty query) with ids and state.19    public func findTasks(query: String) -> ToolResult {20        let trimmed = query.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)21        let matches: [TaskItem]22        if trimmed.isEmpty {23            matches = executor.tasks.filter { !$0.isDone }24        } else {25            switch executor.resolveTasks(matching: trimmed) {26            case .none: matches = []27            case let .unique(task): matches = [task]28            case let .ambiguous(tasks): matches = tasks29            }30        }31        guard !matches.isEmpty else {32            return ToolResult(33                message: "No task matches '\(trimmed)'. \(openTasksSummary())",34                activity: ToolActivity(kind: .findTasks, parameters: [.query(trimmed)], outcome: .failure(.noMatch(query: trimmed)))35            )36        }37        let lines = matches.map { task in38            "- '\(task.title)' (id: \(task.id.uuidString), category: \(task.category.rawValue), priority: \(task.priority.rawValue), status: \(task.status.rawValue), steps: \(task.completedStepCount)/\(task.steps.count))"39        }40        return ToolResult(41            message: "Found \(matches.count) task(s):\n" + lines.joined(separator: "\n"),42            activity: ToolActivity(kind: .findTasks, parameters: [.query(trimmed)], outcome: .success, taskIDs: matches.map(\.id))43        )44    }45 46    // MARK: - Mutations47 48    /// Creates a task.49    public func addTask(title: String, category: TaskCategory, priority: TaskPriority) -> ToolResult {50        let trimmed = title.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)51        let parameters: [ToolParameter] = [.text(trimmed), .category(category), .priority(priority)]52        do {53            let result = try executor.perform(.addTask(title: trimmed, category: category, priority: priority, origin: .assistant), actor: .assistant)54            let id = result.createdTaskID55            let priorityText = priority == .high ? "high" : "normal"56            return ToolResult(57                message: "Added '\(trimmed)' to \(category.rawValue) with \(priorityText) priority.",58                activity: ToolActivity(kind: .addTask, parameters: [.task(title: trimmed, id: id), .category(category), .priority(priority)], outcome: .success, taskIDs: id.map { [$0] } ?? [])59            )60        } catch WorkspaceError.emptyTitle {61            return ToolResult(62                message: "Not added: the title was empty. Ask the user what the task should be called.",63                activity: ToolActivity(kind: .addTask, parameters: parameters, outcome: .failure(.emptyTitle))64            )65        } catch {66            return failure(.addTask, parameters, error)67        }68    }69 70    /// Sets a task's priority (covers prioritise and deprioritise).71    public func setTaskPriority(query: String, priority: TaskPriority) -> ToolResult {72        withUniqueTask(query, kind: .setPriority, extra: [.priority(priority)]) { task in73            guard task.priority != priority else {74                return ("'\(task.title)' is already \(priority.rawValue) priority. No change made.", .unchanged)75            }76            try executor.perform(.setPriority(ids: [task.id], priority), actor: .assistant)77            return ("Marked '\(task.title)' as \(priority.rawValue) priority.", .success)78        }79    }80 81    /// Marks a task as done.82    public func completeTask(query: String) -> ToolResult {83        withUniqueTask(query, kind: .completeTask) { task in84            guard !task.isDone else { return ("'\(task.title)' is already done. No change made.", .unchanged) }85            try executor.perform(.setStatus(ids: [task.id], .done), actor: .assistant)86            return ("Marked '\(task.title)' as done.", .success)87        }88    }89 90    /// Deletes a task. The user can undo it.91    public func deleteTask(query: String) -> ToolResult {92        withUniqueTask(query, kind: .deleteTask) { task in93            try executor.perform(.deleteTasks(ids: [task.id]), actor: .assistant)94            return ("Deleted '\(task.title)'. The user can undo this from the board.", .success)95        }96    }97 98    // MARK: - Helpers99 100    /// Resolves `query` to exactly one task, then runs `body`. Reports none/ambiguous truthfully.101    private func withUniqueTask(102        _ query: String,103        kind: ToolKind,104        extra: [ToolParameter] = [],105        body: (TaskItem) throws -> (String, ToolOutcome)106    ) -> ToolResult {107        let trimmed = query.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)108        switch executor.resolveTasks(matching: trimmed) {109        case .none:110            return ToolResult(111                message: "No task matches '\(trimmed)'. Nothing was changed. \(openTasksSummary())",112                activity: ToolActivity(kind: kind, parameters: [.query(trimmed)] + extra, outcome: .failure(.noMatch(query: trimmed)))113            )114        case let .ambiguous(tasks):115            let titles = tasks.map(\.title)116            let list = titles.map { "'\($0)'" }.joined(separator: ", ")117            return ToolResult(118                message: "Ambiguous: '\(trimmed)' matches \(list).
