"There are no open tasks." : "Open tasks: \(open.joined(separator: ", "))."148    }149}

  4. Step 4

    Add the remaining operations: layout, accent colour, tile colour (keeping the glyph) and checklist steps.

    WorkspaceToolbox.swift
    ⋯1import Foundation2import os3 4/// The tools' shared logic: resolve tasks, issue `WorkspaceCommand`s as `.assistant`, and report5/// truthfully what happened — including "no match", "ambiguous" and "already done".6///7/// Used by the Foundation Models tool adapters and by `ScriptedEngine`, so both paths behave identically.8@MainActor9public final class WorkspaceToolbox: Sendable {10    private let executor: any WorkspaceCommandExecutor11 12    public init(executor: any WorkspaceCommandExecutor) {13        self.executor = executor14    }15 16    // MARK: - Lookup17 18    /// Lists tasks matching `query` (or all open tasks for an empty query) with ids and state.19    public func findTasks(query: String) -> ToolResult {20        let trimmed = query.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)21        let matches: [TaskItem]22        if trimmed.isEmpty {23            matches = executor.tasks.filter { !$0.isDone }24        } else {25            switch executor.resolveTasks(matching: trimmed) {26            case .none: matches = []27            case let .unique(task): matches = [task]28            case let .ambiguous(tasks): matches = tasks29            }30        }31        guard !matches.isEmpty else {32            return ToolResult(33                message: "No task matches '\(trimmed)'. \(openTasksSummary())",34                activity: ToolActivity(kind: .findTasks, parameters: [.query(trimmed)], outcome: .failure(.noMatch(query: trimmed)))35            )36        }37        let lines = matches.map { task in38            "- '\(task.title)' (id: \(task.id.uuidString), category: \(task.category.rawValue), priority: \(task.priority.rawValue), status: \(task.status.rawValue), steps: \(task.completedStepCount)/\(task.steps.count))"39        }40        return ToolResult(41            message: "Found \(matches.count) task(s):\n" + lines.joined(separator: "\n"),42            activity: ToolActivity(kind: .findTasks, parameters: [.query(trimmed)], outcome: .success, taskIDs: matches.map(\.id))43        )44    }45 46    // MARK: - Mutations47 48    /// Creates a task.49    public func addTask(title: String, category: TaskCategory, priority: TaskPriority) -> ToolResult {50        let trimmed = title.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)51        let parameters: [ToolParameter] = [.text(trimmed), .category(category), .priority(priority)]52        do {53            let result = try executor.perform(.addTask(title: trimmed, category: category, priority: priority, origin: .assistant), actor: .assistant)54            let id = result.createdTaskID55            let priorityText = priority == .high ? "high" : "normal"56            return ToolResult(57                message: "Added '\(trimmed)' to \(category.rawValue) with \(priorityText) priority.",58                activity: ToolActivity(kind: .addTask, parameters: [.task(title: trimmed, id: id), .category(category), .priority(priority)], outcome: .success, taskIDs: id.map { [$0] } ?? [])59            )60        } catch WorkspaceError.emptyTitle {61            return ToolResult(62                message: "Not added: the title was empty. Ask the user what the task should be called.",63                activity: ToolActivity(kind: .addTask, parameters: parameters, outcome: .failure(.emptyTitle))64            )65        } catch {66            return failure(.addTask, parameters, error)67        }68    }69 70    /// Sets a task's priority (covers prioritise and deprioritise).71    public func setTaskPriority(query: String, priority: TaskPriority) -> ToolResult {72        withUniqueTask(query, kind: .setPriority, extra: [.priority(priority)]) { task in73            guard task.priority != priority else {74                return ("'\(task.title)' is already \(priority.rawValue) priority. No change made.", .unchanged)75            }76            try executor.perform(.setPriority(ids: [task.id], priority), actor: .assistant)77            return ("Marked '\(task.title)' as \(priority.rawValue) priority.", .success)78        }79    }80 81    /// Marks a task as done.82    public func completeTask(query: String) -> ToolResult {83        withUniqueTask(query, kind: .completeTask) { task in84            guard !task.isDone else { return ("'\(task.title)' is already done. No change made.", .unchanged) }85            try executor.perform(.setStatus(ids: [task.id], .done), actor: .assistant)86            return ("Marked '\(task.title)' as done.", .success)87        }88    }89 90    /// Deletes a task. The user can undo it.91    public func deleteTask(query: String) -> ToolResult {92        withUniqueTask(query, kind: .deleteTask) { task in93            try executor.perform(.deleteTasks(ids: [task.id]), actor: .assistant)94            return ("Deleted '\(task.title)'. The user can undo this from the board.", .success)95        }96    }97 98    /// Switches the board layout.99    public func switchLayout(_ layout: BoardLayout) -> ToolResult {100        let parameters: [ToolParameter] = [.layout(layout)]101        guard executor.preferences.layout != layout else {102            return ToolResult(103                message: "The board is already in \(layout.rawValue) layout. No change made.",104                activity: ToolActivity(kind: .switchLayout, parameters: parameters, outcome: .unchanged)105            )106        }107        do {108            try executor.perform(.setLayout(layout), actor: .assistant)109            return ToolResult(110                message: "Switched the board to \(layout.rawValue) layout.",111                activity: ToolActivity(kind: .switchLayout, parameters: parameters, outcome: .success)112            )113        } catch {114            return failure(.switchLayout, parameters, error)115        }116    }117 118    /// Changes the app's accent colour.119    public func setAccentColor(_ theme: AccentTheme) -> ToolResult {120        let parameters: [ToolParameter] = [.accent(theme)]121        guard executor.preferences.accent != theme else {122            return ToolResult(123                message: "The accent colour is already \(theme.rawValue). No change made.",124                activity: ToolActivity(kind: .setAccentColor, parameters: parameters, outcome: .unchanged)125            )126        }127        do {128            try executor.perform(.setAccent(theme), actor: .assistant)129            return ToolResult(130                message: "Changed the accent colour to \(theme.rawValue).",131                activity: ToolActivity(kind: .setAccentColor, parameters: parameters, outcome: .success)132            )133        } catch {134            return failure(.setAccentColor, parameters, error)135        }136    }137 138    /// Changes a task tile's colour, keeping its glyph.139    public func setTaskColor(query: String, color: TileColor) -> ToolResult {140        withUniqueTask(query, kind: .setTaskColor, extra: [.color(color)]) { task in141            let current = task.resolvedAppearance142            guard current.color != color else {143                return ("'\(task.title)' is already \(color.rawValue). No change made.", .unchanged)144            }145            try executor.perform(.setAppearance(id: task.id, TileAppearance(color: color, glyph: current.glyph)), actor: .assistant)146            return ("Changed '\(task.title)' to \(color.rawValue).", .success)147        }148    }149 150    /// Adds a checklist step to a task.151    public func addStep(query: String, stepTitle: String) -> ToolResult {152        let step = stepTitle.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)153        return withUniqueTask(query, kind: .addStep, extra: [.text(step)]) { task in154            guard !step.isEmpty else { throw WorkspaceError.emptyTitle }155            try executor.perform(.addStep(taskID: task.id, title: step), actor: .assistant)156            return ("Added step '\(step)' to '\(task.title)'.", .success)157        }158    }159 160    // MARK: - Helpers161 162    /// Resolves `query` to exactly one task, then runs `body`. Reports none/ambiguous truthfully.⋯163    private func withUniqueTask(164        _ query: String,165        kind: ToolKind,166        extra: [ToolParameter] = [],167        body: (TaskItem) throws -> (String, ToolOutcome)168    ) -> ToolResult {169        let trimmed = query.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)170        switch executor.resolveTasks(matching: trimmed) {171        case .none:172            return ToolResult(173                message: "No task matches '\(trimmed)'. Nothing was changed. \(openTasksSummary())",174                activity: ToolActivity(kind: kind, parameters: [.query(trimmed)] + extra, outcome: .failure(.noMatch(query: trimmed)))175            )176        case let .ambiguous(tasks):177            let titles = tasks.map(\.title)178            let list = titles.map { "'\($0)'" }.joined(separator: ", ")179            return ToolResult(180                message: "Ambiguous: '\(trimmed)' matches \(list). Nothing was changed. Ask the user which one they mean.",181                activity: ToolActivity(kind: kind, parameters: [.query(trimmed)] + extra, outcome: .failure(.ambiguous(query: trimmed, candidates: titles)), taskIDs: tasks.map(\.id))182            )183        case let .unique(task):184            let parameters = [ToolParameter.task(title: task.title, id: task.id)] + extra185            do {186                let (message, outcome) = try body(task)187                return ToolResult(message: message, activity: ToolActivity(kind: kind, parameters: parameters, outcome: outcome, taskIDs: [task.id]))188            } catch WorkspaceError.emptyTitle {189                return ToolResult(190                    message: "Nothing was changed: the text was empty.",191                    activity: ToolActivity(kind: kind, parameters: parameters, outcome: .failure(.emptyTitle), taskIDs: [task.id])192                )193            } catch {194                return failure(kind, parameters, error)195            }196        }197    }198 199    private func failure(_ kind: ToolKind, _ parameters: [ToolParameter], _ error: any Error) -> ToolResult {200        Log.agent.error("Tool \(kind.rawValue, privacy: .public) failed: \(String(describing: error), privacy: .public)")201        return ToolResult(202            message: "The change failed and nothing was modified (\(String(describing: error))).",203            activity: ToolActivity(kind: kind, parameters: parameters, outcome: .failure(.rejected(String(describing: error))))204        )205    }206 207    private func openTasksSummary() -> String {208        let open = executor.tasks.filter { !$0.isDone }.map { "'\($0.title)'" }209        return open.isEmpty ? "There are no open tasks." : "Open tasks: \(open.joined(separator: ", "))."210    }211}

Section 3

Wrap the Toolbox as Tools

Now the Foundation Models part. Each tool has a name, a description the model reads, @Generable arguments it must fill in, and a call that runs the toolbox.

  1. Step 1

    In Domain/Services/Assistant/Tools, create GenerableArguments.swift. These @Generable enums mirror domain enums, so the model can only choose valid values. .domain converts back.

    GenerableArguments.swift
    1import FoundationModels2 3/// Task category as a constrained model argument.4@Generable5enum CategoryArgument: String, CaseIterable {6    case development, testing, design, operations7 8    var domain: TaskCategory { TaskCategory(rawValue: rawValue) ?? .development }9}10 11/// Task priority as a constrained model argument.12@Generable13enum PriorityArgument: String, CaseIterable {14    case normal, high15 16    var domain: TaskPriority { self == .high ? .high : .normal }17}18 19/// Board layout as a constrained model argument.20@Generable21enum LayoutArgument: String, CaseIterable {22    case grid, list, focus, board23 24    var domain: BoardLayout { BoardLayout(rawValue: rawValue) ?? .grid }25}26 27/// Accent theme as a constrained model argument.28@Generable29enum AccentArgument: String, CaseIterable {30    case indigo, blue, teal, green, orange, red, purple31 32    var domain: AccentTheme { AccentTheme(rawValue: rawValue) ?? .indigo }33}34 35/// Tile colour as a constrained model argument.36@Generable37enum TileColorArgument: String, CaseIterable {38    case red, orange, yellow, green, mint, teal, cyan, blue, indigo, purple, pink, gray39 40    var domain: TileColor { TileColor(rawValue: rawValue) ?? .blue }41}

  2. Step 2

    Create ToolActivityRecorder.swift. Tools run inside the model's response; the recorder forwards each activity to whichever response stream is current, so the chat can show it immediately.

    ToolActivityRecorder.swift
    1 2/// Forwards tool activity from tool calls to the engine's current response stream.3@MainActor4public final class ToolActivityRecorder: Sendable {5    /// Receives each activity while a response is streaming.6    var onActivity: ((ToolActivity) -> Void)?7 8    public init() {}9 10    func record(_ activity: ToolActivity) {11        onActivity?(activity)12    }13}

  3. Step 3

    Create WorkspaceTools.swift with make(toolbox:recorder:), the shared run helper and the first two tools. run hops to the main actor, performs the operation, records the activity and returns the message.

    WorkspaceTools.swift
    1import FoundationModels2 3/// Builds the assistant's tool set over a toolbox and recorder.4enum WorkspaceTools {5    static func make(toolbox: WorkspaceToolbox, recorder: ToolActivityRecorder) -> [any Tool] {6        [7            FindTasksTool(toolbox: toolbox, recorder: recorder),8            AddTaskTool(toolbox: toolbox, recorder: recorder),9        ]10    }11}12 13/// Runs a toolbox operation on the main actor, reports its activity, and returns the message.14private func run(_ recorder: ToolActivityRecorder, _ operation: @MainActor () -> ToolResult) async -> String {15    await MainActor.run {16        let result = operation()17        recorder.record(result.activity)18        return result.message19    }20}21 22/// Looks up tasks by title words before acting.23struct FindTasksTool: Tool {24    let name = "findTasks"25    let description = "Looks up tasks by title. Returns titles, ids, category, priority and status. Use an empty query to list all open tasks."26    let toolbox: WorkspaceToolbox27    let recorder: ToolActivityRecorder28 29    @Generable30    struct Arguments {31        @Guide(description: "Words from the task title, or empty to list all open tasks")32        var query: String33    }34 35    func call(arguments: Arguments) async throws -> String {36        await run(recorder) { toolbox.findTasks(query: arguments.query) }37    }38}39 40/// Creates a task.41struct AddTaskTool: Tool {42    let name = "addTask"43    let description = "Creates a new task."44    let toolbox: WorkspaceToolbox45    let recorder: ToolActivityRecorder46 47    @Generable48    struct Arguments {49        @Guide(description: "Short task title in title case, e.g. 'Code Review'")50        var title: String51        var category: CategoryArgument52        var priority: PriorityArgument53    }54 55    func call(arguments: Arguments) async throws -> String {56        await run(recorder) {57            toolbox.addTask(title: arguments.title, category: arguments.category.domain, priority: arguments.priority.domain)58        }59    }60}

  4. Step 4

    Add the other seven tools. Each is a few lines. Note DeleteTaskTool's description: "Only use when the user explicitly asks". Descriptions are where you set the model's boundaries.

Tutorial 6 of 8 · 30 min

The Assistant Engine

Hide the language model behind a protocol. The real engine keeps one long-lived Foundation Models session and streams events as it works; a scripted engine stands in when Apple Intelligence isn't available, and an automatic engine chooses between them on every prompt.

Download Project Files

Section 1

Define the Engine Contract

The UI never talks to Foundation Models directly. It sends a prompt to an AssistantEngine and receives a stream of events: tool calls as they happen, the reply as it grows, and the final text. Any engine that produces those events will do, including a fake one in tests.

  1. Step 1

    Create Domain/Models/AssistantEvent.swift. partialText carries the reply so far (cumulative, not a delta), which is what Foundation Models' streaming snapshots provide. Copy AssistantAvailability.swift and AssistantError.swift from the download.

    AssistantEvent.swift
    1/// Events streamed by an `AssistantEngine` while it answers a prompt.2public enum AssistantEvent: Hashable, Sendable {3    /// A tool ran (successfully or not).4    case toolCalled(ToolActivity)5    /// The reply so far (cumulative, not a delta).6    case partialText(String)7    /// The final reply.8    case completed(String)9}

  2. Step 2

    Create Domain/Store/AssistantEngine.swift. simulationReason is non-nil only for the stand-in, so the UI can always label it honestly. Cancelling the task that consumes the stream cancels generation.

    AssistantEngine.swift
    1/// An assistant that turns natural-language prompts into workspace commands via tools.2///3/// Implemented by `FoundationModelsEngine` (Apple Intelligence) and `ScriptedEngine` (simulated stand-in).4@MainActor5public protocol AssistantEngine: AnyObject, Sendable {6    /// Whether this engine can respond right now.7    var availability: AssistantAvailability { get }8    /// Non-nil when this is the simulated stand-in, explaining why the real model isn't used.9    var simulationReason: AssistantUnavailableReason? { get }10    /// Whether a response is in flight.11    var isResponding: Bool { get }12    /// Sends a prompt. The stream yields tool calls and text, then finishes or throws `AssistantError`.13    /// Cancelling the consuming task cancels generation.14    func send(_ prompt: String) -> AsyncThrowingStream<AssistantEvent, any Error>15    /// Forgets the conversation and starts a fresh session.16    func reset() async17    /// Loads resources ahead of the first prompt.18    func prewarm() async19}

Section 2

Talk to Apple Intelligence

The real engine keeps one LanguageModelSession for the whole conversation, so the model remembers context: "now undo that" means something. It streams the reply with streamResponse(to:) while the tools report their activity through the recorder.

In Domain/Services/Assistant, add a FoundationModels folder.

  1. Step 1

    Create AssistantInstructions.swift. Short and specific works best on the on-device model: which tools exist, to pass the user's words as the query, to ask when a match is ambiguous, and never to claim something happened unless a tool said so.

    AssistantInstructions.swift
    1/// System instructions for the on-device model.2enum AssistantInstructions {3    static let text = """4    You are the assistant inside a personal task workspace app. You change the workspace only by calling tools.5    Tools: findTasks looks up tasks; addTask, setTaskPriority, completeTask, deleteTask, setTaskColor and addStep change tasks; \6    switchLayout and setAccentColor change how the app looks.7    Rules:8    - When a request names a task, pass the user's words as the query. If a tool says the match is ambiguous, ask the user which task they mean.9    - Read every tool result. Only say something happened if a tool result says it did. If a tool reports no match or no change, say so.10    - Only delete tasks when the user clearly asks. Mention that deletions can be undone.11    - Reply in one or two short sentences. Don't list tool names or ids.12    """13}

  2. Step 2

    Create AssistantErrorMapping.swift. It maps Foundation Models errors and availability to the app's own AssistantError and AssistantAvailability, so each failure gets specific, friendly copy. It handles iOS 26's GenerationError and recognises iOS 27's error types by name.

    AssistantErrorMapping.swift
    1import Foundation2import FoundationModels3 4/// Maps Foundation Models errors (iOS 26 `GenerationError` and iOS 27 `LanguageModelError`) to `AssistantError`.5enum AssistantErrorMapping {6    static func map(_ error: any Error) -> AssistantError {7        if let mapped = error as? AssistantError { return mapped }8        if #available(iOS 27.0, *), let mapped = mapModern(error) { return mapped }9        if let generation = error as? LanguageModelSession.GenerationError { return map(generation) }10        return .other(String(describing: error))11    }12 13    /// iOS 26 error type (deprecated in iOS 27 but still the type thrown on iOS 26).14    static func map(_ error: LanguageModelSession.GenerationError) -> AssistantError {15        switch error {16        case .exceededContextWindowSize: .contextWindowExceeded17        case .assetsUnavailable: .assetsUnavailable18        case .guardrailViolation: .guardrailViolation19        case .unsupportedLanguageOrLocale: .unsupportedLanguage20        case .rateLimited: .rateLimited21        case .concurrentRequests: .busy22        case .refusal: .refusal23        case .unsupportedGuide, .decodingFailure: .other(String(describing: error))24        @unknown default: .other(String(describing: error))25        }26    }27 28    /// Reflective mapping for iOS 27 error types when running on newer OS versions.29    /// Uses type reflection so the package compiles against the current iOS 26 SDK without missing-type errors.30    private static func mapModern(_ error: any Error) -> AssistantError? {31        let typeName = String(reflecting: type(of: error))32        let desc = String(describing: error)33 34        if typeName.contains("LanguageModelError") {35            if desc.contains("contextSizeExceeded") || desc.contains("exceededContextWindowSize") {36                return .contextWindowExceeded37            }38            if desc.contains("rateLimited") { return .rateLimited }39            if desc.contains("guardrailViolation") { return .guardrailViolation }40            if desc.contains("refusal") { return .refusal }41            if desc.contains("unsupportedLanguage") { return .unsupportedLanguage }42            if desc.contains("timeout") { return .timeout }43            return .other(desc)44        }45 46        if typeName.contains("LanguageModelSession") && typeName.contains("Error") {47            if desc.contains("concurrentRequests") { return .busy }48            return .other(desc)49        }50 51        if typeName.contains("SystemLanguageModel") && typeName.contains("Error") {52            if desc.contains("assetsUnavailable") { return .assetsUnavailable }53            return .other(desc)54        }55 56        return nil57    }58 59    /// Maps the system model's availability.60    static func map(_ availability: SystemLanguageModel.Availability) -> AssistantAvailability {61        switch availability {62        case .available: .available63        case let .unavailable(reason):64            switch reason {65            case .deviceNotEligible: .unavailable(.deviceNotEligible)66            case .appleIntelligenceNotEnabled: .unavailable(.appleIntelligenceNotEnabled)67            case .modelNotReady: .unavailable(.modelNotReady)68            @unknown default: .unavailable(.modelNotReady)69            }70        }71    }72}

  3. Step 3

    Create FoundationModelsEngine.swift with the session and availability. The tools are built once, around a toolbox and a recorder. Availability also checks supportsLocale(), because the model may be ready but not for the user's language.

    FoundationModelsEngine.swift
    1import Foundation2import FoundationModels3import os4 5/// The Apple Intelligence assistant: one long-lived `LanguageModelSession` with the workspace tools,6/// streaming replies and reporting each tool call as it happens.7@MainActor8public final class FoundationModelsEngine {9    private let model: SystemLanguageModel10    private let tools: [any Tool]11    private let recorder: ToolActivityRecorder12    private var session: LanguageModelSession13 14    public init(executor: any WorkspaceCommandExecutor, model: SystemLanguageModel = .default) {15        self.model = model16        recorder = ToolActivityRecorder()17        tools = WorkspaceTools.make(toolbox: WorkspaceToolbox(executor: executor), recorder: recorder)18        session = Self.makeSession(model: model, tools: tools, summary: nil)19    }20 21    public var availability: AssistantAvailability {22        let mapped = AssistantErrorMapping.map(model.availability)23        if mapped.isAvailable, !model.supportsLocale() { return .unavailable(.unsupportedLanguage) }24        return mapped25    }26 27    public var simulationReason: AssistantUnavailableReason? { nil }28 29    public var isResponding: Bool { session.isResponding }30 31    public func reset() async {32        session = Self.makeSession(model: model, tools: tools, summary: nil)33    }34 35    public func prewarm() async {36        guard availability.isAvailable else { return }37        session.prewarm()38    }39 40    private static func makeSession(model: SystemLanguageModel, tools: [any Tool], summary: String?) -> LanguageModelSession {41        var instructions = AssistantInstructions.text42        if let summary {43            instructions += "\nEarlier in this conversation (summary):\n\(summary)"44        }45        return LanguageModelSession(model: model, tools: tools, instructions: instructions)46    }47}

  4. Step 4

    Add send(_:) and respond(to:continuation:), and conform to AssistantEngine. send returns an AsyncThrowingStream whose termination cancels the work. While responding, the recorder yields .toolCalled events, and each streaming snapshot becomes .partialText. A second prompt while one is running is rejected as .busy.

    FoundationModelsEngine.swift

Section 3

Recover When the Context Fills Up

The on-device model has a small context window. Rather than failing for good, the engine starts a new session and carries a short summary of the last exchanges in its instructions.

  1. Step 1

    Remember the last four exchanges. When the model reports contextWindowExceeded, restartWithSummary() builds a new session whose instructions end with a summary of the last two. The user sees one friendly error and can simply ask again.

    FoundationModelsEngine.swift

      guard availability.isAvailable else { return }50        session.prewarm()51    }52 53    // MARK: - Responding54 55    private func respond(to prompt: String, continuation: AsyncThrowingStream<AssistantEvent, any Error>.Continuation) async {56        if case let .unavailable(reason) = availability {57            continuation.finish(throwing: AssistantError.unavailable(reason))58            return59        }60        guard !session.isResponding else {61            continuation.finish(throwing: AssistantError.busy)62            return63 snapshot in session.streamResponse(to: prompt) {70                try Task.checkCancellation()71                reply = snapshot.content72                continuation.yield(.partialText(reply))73 }90    }91 92    /// Starts a new session carrying a short summary of the latest exchanges.93    private func restartWithSummary() {94        let summary = recentTurns.suffix(2)95            .map { "User asked: \($0.prompt.prefix(200)) — You replied: \($0.reply.prefix(200))" }96            .joined(separator: "\n")97        session = Self.makeSession(model: model, tools: tools, summary: summary.isEmpty ? nil : summary)98        Log.agent.info("Context window exceeded; started a new session with a summary")99    }100 101    private static func makeSession(model: SystemLanguageModel, tools: [any Tool], summary: String?) -> LanguageModelSession {⋯102        var instructions = AssistantInstructions.text103        if let summary {104            instructions += "\nEarlier in this Section 4

Keep Working Without Apple Intelligence

On a simulator or a device without Apple Intelligence, a rule-based engine takes over. It runs the same toolbox, so the board changes exactly as it would with the model, and the UI labels it "Simulated" everywhere.

  1. Step 1

    Copy the Scripted folder from the download: ScriptedIntent.swift, ScriptedIntentParser.swift and this file. The parser turns phrases like "prioritise all testing tasks and use List view" into intents; ScriptedEngine runs them through the toolbox and streams a short, truthful reply word by word.

    ScriptedEngine.swift
    1import Foundation2 3/// A deterministic stand-in for the language model, used when Apple Intelligence isn't available,4/// in previews and in UI tests. It runs the same toolbox code paths as the real tools.5/// The UI must always label it as a simulated assistant.6@MainActor7public final class ScriptedEngine: AssistantEngine {8    private let toolbox: WorkspaceToolbox9    private let executor: any WorkspaceCommandExecutor10    private let reason: AssistantUnavailableReason11    private let wordDelay: Duration12    public private(set) var isResponding = false13 14    /// - Parameters:15    ///   - reason: Why the simulated assistant is in use (shown in the UI).16    ///   - wordDelay: Delay between streamed words; use `.zero` in tests.17    public init(executor: any WorkspaceCommandExecutor, reason: AssistantUnavailableReason, wordDelay: Duration = .milliseconds(25)) {18        self.executor = executor19        toolbox = WorkspaceToolbox(executor: executor)20        self.reason = reason21        self.wordDelay = wordDelay22    }23 24    public var availability: AssistantAvailability { .available }25    public var simulationReason: AssistantUnavailableReason? { reason }26 27    public func send(_ prompt: String) -> AsyncThrowingStream<AssistantEvent, any Error> {28        AsyncThrowingStream { continuation in29            let task = Task { @MainActor in30                await self.respond(to: prompt, continuation: continuation)31            }32            continuation.onTermination = { _ in task.cancel() }33        }34    }35 36    public func reset() async {}37    public func prewarm() async {}38 39    private func respond(to prompt: String, continuation: AsyncThrowingStream<AssistantEvent, any Error>.Continuation) async {40        guard !isResponding else {41            continuation.finish(throwing: AssistantError.busy)42            return43        }44        isResponding = true45        defer { isResponding = false }46 47        let results = ScriptedIntentParser.parse(prompt).flatMap(run)48        for result in results {49            continuation.yield(.toolCalled(result.activity))50        }51        let reply = Self.reply(for: results)52        do {53            var streamed = ""54            for word in reply.split(separator: " ", omittingEmptySubsequences: false) {55                try Task.checkCancellation()56                streamed += streamed.isEmpty ? String(word) : " " + word57                continuation.yield(.partialText(streamed))58                if wordDelay > .zero { try await Task.sleep(for: wordDelay) }59            }60            continuation.yield(.completed(reply))61            continuation.finish()62        } catch {63            continuation.finish(throwing: CancellationError())64        }65    }66 67    private func run(_ intent: ScriptedIntent) -> [ToolResult] {68        switch intent {69        case let .setPriority(query, priority): [toolbox.setTaskPriority(query: query, priority: priority)]70        case let .setCategoryPriority(category, priority):71            executor.tasks72                .filter { $0.category == category && !$0.isDone }73                .map { toolbox.setTaskPriority(query: $0.id.uuidString, priority: priority) }74        case let .complete(query): [toolbox.completeTask(query: query)]75        case let .delete(query): [toolbox.deleteTask(query: query)]76        case let .addTask(title, category, priority): [toolbox.addTask(title: title, category: category, priority: priority)]77        case let .addStep(query, step): [toolbox.addStep(query: query, stepTitle: step)]78        case let .switchLayout(layout): [toolbox.switchLayout(layout)]79        case let .setAccent(theme): [toolbox.setAccentColor(theme)]80        case let .setTaskColor(query, color): [toolbox.setTaskColor(query: query, color: color)]81        case let .find(query): [toolbox.findTasks(query: query)]82        }83    }84 85    /// Builds a short, truthful reply from what the tools reported.86    static func reply(for results: [ToolResult]) -> String {87        guard !results.isEmpty else {88            return "I'm a simulated assistant, so I only understand simple requests like “Prioritise the network refactor”, “Switch to Board view” or “Add a task for code review”."89        }90        let done = results.filter { $0.activity.succeeded }.map(\.activity)91        let failures = results.filter { !$0.activity.succeeded }.map(\.activity)92        var sentences: [String] = []93        if !done.isEmpty {94            sentences.append("Done — I " + ListFormatter.localizedString(byJoining: done.map(phrase)) + ".")95        }96        for failure in failures {97            sentences.append(sentence(for: failure))98        }99        return sentences.joined(separator: " ")100    }101 102    private static func phrase(_ activity: ToolActivity) -> String {103        let task = activity.parameters.lazy.compactMap { if case let .task(title, _) = $0 { "“\(title)”" } else { nil } }.first ?? "it"104        switch activity.kind {105        case .findTasks: return "found \(activity.taskIDs.count) matching task(s)"106        case .addTask: return "added \(task)"107        case .setPriority:108            return activity.parameters.contains(.priority(.normal)) ? "removed priority from \(task)" : "prioritised \(task)"109        case .completeTask: return "completed \(task)"110        case .deleteTask: return "deleted \(task) (you can undo this)"111        case .switchLayout:112            let layout = activity.parameters.lazy.compactMap { if case let .layout(layout) = $0 { layout.rawValue.capitalized } else { nil } }.first ?? ""113            return "switched to \(layout)"114        case .setAccentColor:115            let theme = activity.parameters.lazy.compactMap { if case let .accent(theme) = $0 { theme.rawValue } else { nil } }.first ?? ""116            return "changed the accent colour to \(theme)"117        case .setTaskColor: return "recoloured \(task)"118        case .addStep: return "added a step to \(task)"119        }120    }121 122    private static func sentence(for activity: ToolActivity) -> String {123        switch activity.outcome {124        case .success: return ""125        case .unchanged:126            let task = activity.parameters.lazy.compactMap { if case let .task(title, _) = $0 { "“\(title)”" } else { nil } }.first127            return task.map { "\($0) didn't need changing." } ?? "That was already set."128        case let .failure(.noMatch(query)): return "I couldn't find a task matching “\(query)”."129        case let .failure(.ambiguous(query, candidates)):130            return "“\(query)” matches \(ListFormatter.localizedString(byJoining: candidates.map { "“\($0)”" })) — which one did you mean?"131        case .failure(.emptyTitle): return "I need a title for that."132        case .failure(.rejected): return "Something went wrong, so nothing was changed."133        }134    }135}

  2. Step 2

    Create AutomaticAssistantEngine.swift. It checks availability on every prompt, so the real model takes over as soon as it finishes downloading, without restarting the app.

    AutomaticAssistantEngine.swift
    1 2/// Uses Apple Intelligence when it's available and the scripted stand-in otherwise,3/// re-checking availability on every prompt (e.g. once the model finishes downloading).4@MainActor5public final class AutomaticAssistantEngine: AssistantEngine {6    private let primary: FoundationModelsEngine7    private let executor: any WorkspaceCommandExecutor8    private var fallback: ScriptedEngine?9 10    public init(executor: any WorkspaceCommandExecutor) {11        self.executor = executor12        primary = FoundationModelsEngine(executor: executor)13    }14 15    private var active: any AssistantEngine {16        if case let .unavailable(reason) = primary.availability {17            if let fallback, fallback.simulationReason == reason { return fallback }18            let engine = ScriptedEngine(executor: executor, reason: reason)19            fallback = engine20            return engine21        }22        return primary23    }24 25    public var availability: AssistantAvailability { active.availability }26    public var simulationReason: AssistantUnavailableReason? { active.simulationReason }27    public var isResponding: Bool { primary.isResponding || (fallback?.isResponding ?? false) }28 29    public func send(_ prompt: String) -> AsyncThrowingStream<AssistantEvent, any Error> {30        active.send(prompt)31    }32 33    public func reset() async {34        await primary.reset()35        await fallback?.reset()36    }37 38    public func prewarm() async {39        await active.prewarm()40    }41}

The Assistant Panel

Turn the engine's event stream into a conversation: user messages, action blocks for every tool call, and a reply that streams in. Then connect the assistant to the app, with a pill above the tab bar that opens it over the live board.

Section 1

Model the Conversation

AssistantViewModel consumes events and keeps an ordered transcript. Tool calls that arrive while the reply is streaming are inserted before the reply, so the chat always reads "what I did, then what I say".

  1. Step 1

    Copy the ViewModels/Assistant folder from the download. TranscriptItem is the core of it: a user message, an assistant reply (still streaming or not), an action, or a notice such as an error.

    TranscriptItem.swift
    1import Foundation2 3/// One entry in the assistant transcript.4public struct TranscriptItem: Identifiable, Hashable, Sendable {5    /// What the entry shows.6    public enum Content: Hashable, Sendable {7        case user(String)8        /// Assistant reply text; `isStreaming` while it's still arriving.9        case assistant(String, isStreaming: Bool)10        case action(ToolActivity)11        case notice(AssistantNotice)12    }13 14    public let id: UUID15    public let date: Date16    public var content: Content17 18    public init(id: UUID = UUID(), date: Date = .now, content: Content) {19        self.id = id20        self.date = date21        self.content = content22    }23}24 25/// A system note in the transcript (errors, stops).26public enum AssistantNotice: Hashable, Sendable {27    case error(AssistantError)28    case stopped29}

  2. Step 2

    Create ViewModels/AssistantViewModel.swift. send() appends the user's message, starts the engine's stream and handles each event. Errors become friendly notices in the transcript instead of alerts.

Ignored while responding or when the draft is blank.61    public func send() {62        let prompt = draft.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)63        guard !prompt.isEmpty, phase == .idle else { return }64        draft = ""65        items.append(TranscriptItem(date: now(), content: .user(prompt)))66        phase = .responding67        refreshAvailability()68 69        let stream = engine.send(prompt)70        responseTask = Task { [weak self] in71            do {72                for try await event in stream {73                    guard let self, !Task.isCancelled else { break }74                    self.handle(event)75                }76                self?.finish(cancelled: Task.isCancelled)77            } catch {78                self?.fail(error)79            }80        }81    }82 83    /// Stops the current response.84    public func cancel() {85        guard phase == .responding else { return }86        responseTask?.cancel()87        responseTask = nil88        finish(cancelled: true)89    }90 91    /// Clears the conversation and resets the engine's session. Never touches tasks or layout.92    public func clear() {93        cancel()94        items.removeAll()95        lastActivity = nil96        Task { await engine.reset() }97    }98 99    // MARK: - Events100 101    private func handle(_ event: AssistantEvent) {⋯102        switch event {103        case let .toolCalled(activity):104            lastActivity = activity105            let item = TranscriptItem(date: now(), content: .action(activity))106            if let index = streamingIndex {107                items.insert(item, at: index)108            } else {109                items.append(item)110            }111        case let .partialText(text):112            updateReply(text, isStreaming: true)113        case let .completed(text):114            updateReply(text, isStreaming: false)115        }116    }117 118    private var streamingIndex: Int? {119        items.lastIndex { item in120            if case .assistant(_, true) = item.content { return true }121            return false122        }123    }124 125    private func updateReply(_ text: String, isStreaming: Bool) {126        if let index = streamingIndex {127            items[index].content = .assistant(text, isStreaming: isStreaming)128        } else if !text.isEmpty {129            items.append(TranscriptItem(date: now(), content: .assistant(text, isStreaming: isStreaming)))130        }131    }132 133    private func finish(cancelled: Bool) {134        guard phase == .responding else { return }135        if let index = streamingIndex {136            if case let .assistant(text, _) = items[index].content, text.isEmpty {137                items.remove(at: index)138            } else if case let .assistant(text, _) = items[index].content {139                items[index].content = .assistant(text, isStreaming: false)140            }141        }142        if cancelled { items.append(TranscriptItem(date: now(), content: .notice(.stopped))) }143        phase = .idle144        responseTask = nil145    }146 147    private func fail(_ error: any Error) {148        if error is CancellationError {149            finish(cancelled: true)150            return151        }152        let mapped = error as? AssistantError ?? .other(String(describing: error))153        Log.agent.error("Assistant response failed: \(String(describing: mapped), privacy: .public)")154        finish(cancelled: false)155        items.append(TranscriptItem(date: now(), content: .notice(.error(mapped))))156    }157}

Section 2

Show What the Agent Did

Copy Views/Assistant, ViewModels/Settings, Views/Settings and Views/Root/AppCommands.swift from the download. The panel, transcript, composer and suggestion tiles are standard SwiftUI; one view deserves a closer look.

  1. Step 1

    Open TranscriptRow.swift. Each tool call becomes an ActionBlock, a Shortcuts-style card with a verb and token pills. A failed action shows why. The latest successful delete gets an Undo button wired to the scene's undo manager, and tapping a block reveals that task on the board.

    TranscriptRow.swift
    1import SwiftUI2 3/// Renders one transcript entry.4struct TranscriptRow: View {5    let item: TranscriptItem6    let isLatestAction: Bool7    let onSelectTask: (UUID) -> Void8    @Environment(\.undoManager) private var undoManager9 10    var body: some View {11        switch item.content {12        case let .user(text): userBubble(text)13        case let .assistant(text, isStreaming): assistantText(text, isStreaming: isStreaming)14        case let .action(activity): actionBlock(activity)15        case let .notice(notice): noticeRow(notice)16        }17    }18 19    private func userBubble(_ text: String) -> some View {20        HStack {21            Spacer(minLength: Spacing.xxl)22            Text(text)23                .padding(.horizontal, Spacing.s)24                .padding(.vertical, Spacing.xs)25                .foregroundStyle(.white)26                .background(.tint, in: RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 18, style: .continuous))27                .textSelection(.enabled)28        }29        .accessibilityElement(children: .combine)30        .accessibilityLabel(Text("You: \(text)"))31    }32 33    private func assistantText(_ text: String, isStreaming: Bool) -> some View {34        HStack(alignment: .top, spacing: Spacing.xs) {35            Image(systemName: "sparkles")36                .foregroundStyle(.tint)37                .symbolEffect(.pulse, isActive: isStreaming)38                .accessibilityHidden(true)39            Text(text)40                .textSelection(.enabled)41                .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)42        }43        .accessibilityElement(children: .combine)44        .accessibilityLabel(Text("Assistant: \(text)"))45    }46 47    private func actionBlock(_ activity: ToolActivity) -> some View {48        let block = ActionBlock(49            glyph: activity.kind.glyph,50            color: activity.kind.color,51            parts: activity.blockParts,52            failureReason: activity.succeeded ? nil : activity.failureReason,53            accessibilitySentence: activity.spokenSentence54        ) {55            if activity.kind == .deleteTask, activity.succeeded, isLatestAction, undoManager?.canUndo == true {56                Button {57                    undoManager?.undo()58                } label: {59                    Text("Undo")60                }61                .buttonStyle(.bordered)62                .controlSize(.small)63            }64        }65        return Group {66            if let taskID = activity.referencedTaskID, activity.kind != .deleteTask {67                Button { onSelectTask(taskID) } label: { block }68                    .buttonStyle(.plain)69                    .accessibilityHint(Text("Shows this task on the board"))70            } else {71                block72            }73        }74    }75 76    private func noticeRow(_ notice: AssistantNotice) -> some View {77        Group {78            switch notice {79            case .stopped:80                Label { Text("Stopped") } icon: { Image(systemName: "stop.circle") }81                    .foregroundStyle(.secondary)82            case let .error(error):83                Label { Text(AssistantCopy.message(for: error)) } icon: { Image(systemName: "exclamationmark.bubble") }84                    .foregroundStyle(.secondary)85            }86        }87        .font(.footnote)88        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)89    }90}

Section 3

Connect Everything

Three edits finish the app: create the engine, show the assistant from the tab bar, and add keyboard shortcuts.

  1. Step 1

    In AppDependencies, create the engine. UI tests get the scripted engine with no delay; the app gets AutomaticAssistantEngine. Both are wrapped in an AssistantViewModel.

    AppDependencies.swift
    ⋯1import Foundation2import os3 4/// Composition root: builds storage, the store and feature models once per launch.5@MainActor6final class AppDependencies {7    let store: WorkspaceStore8    let board: BoardViewModel9    let assistant: AssistantViewModel10    let router = AppRouter()11    let launch: LaunchConfiguration12 ⋯13    init(launch: LaunchConfiguration = LaunchConfiguration()) {14        self.launch = launch15        let repository: any TaskRepository16        let preferences: any PreferencesStore17        if launch.usesEphemeralStorage {18            repository = InMemoryTaskRepository()19            preferences = InMemoryPreferencesStore()20        } else {21            do {22                repository = try SwiftDataTaskRepository()23            } catch {24                Log.persistence.fault("Falling back to in-memory storage: \(error.localizedDescription, privacy: .public)")25                repository = InMemoryTaskRepository()26            }27            preferences = UserDefaultsPreferencesStore()28        }29        store = WorkspaceStore(repository: repository, preferencesStore: preferences)30        store.undoActionName = UndoActionNames.name(for:)31        board = BoardViewModel(store: store, sortStorage: launch.usesEphemeralStorage ? nil : .standard)32 33        let engine: any AssistantEngine = launch.isUITest34            ? ScriptedEngine(executor: store, reason: .simulatedByConfiguration, wordDelay: .zero)35            : AutomaticAssistantEngine(executor: store)36        assistant = AssistantViewModel(engine: engine)37    }38}

Up nextTesting Without a Model

Tutorial 8 of 8 · 25 min

Testing Without a Model

Because every behaviour is a command, every tool is plain Swift, and every engine is a protocol, you can test the whole agent with no language model, no network and no device. Write Swift Testing tests for the store, the toolbox and the assistant's view model.

Download Project Files

Section 1

Test Commands and Undo

If your project doesn't have a unit test target yet, add one with File › New › Target… › Unit Testing Bundle, choosing Swift Testing. The tests use @testable import WorkspaceAssistant.

  1. Step 1

    Create StoreFixture.swift. It builds a store over in-memory storage with a real UndoManager. Setting groupsByEvent = false and wrapping each command in its own undo group makes undo behave as it does for one tap, without a running app.

    StoreFixture.swift
    1import Foundation2@testable import WorkspaceAssistant3 4/// Builds a store over in-memory storage with a manual-grouping undo manager.5@MainActor6struct StoreFixture {7    let store: WorkspaceStore8    let repository: InMemoryTaskRepository9    let preferences: InMemoryPreferencesStore10    let undoManager: UndoManager11 12    init(tasks: [TaskItem] = SampleData.tasks(now: Date(timeIntervalSince1970: 1_000_000))) {13        repository = InMemoryTaskRepository()14        preferences = InMemoryPreferencesStore()15        store = WorkspaceStore(repository: repository, preferencesStore: preferences, seed: tasks)16        undoManager = UndoManager()17        undoManager.groupsByEvent = false18        store.undoManager = undoManager19    }20 21    /// Performs a command inside its own undo group, as a single user event would.22    @discardableResult23    func perform(_ command: WorkspaceCommand, actor: CommandActor = .user) throws -> CommandResult {24        undoManager.beginUndoGrouping()25        defer { undoManager.endUndoGrouping() }26        return try store.perform(command, actor: actor)27    }28 29    func undo() { undoManager.undo() }30    func redo() { undoManager.redo() }31 32    func task(_ title: String) -> TaskItem? { store.tasks.first { $0.title == title } }33 34    /// Persisted tasks, sorted by sort index.35    func persisted() throws -> [TaskItem] { try repository.fetchAll().sorted { $0.sortIndex < $1.sortIndex } }36}

  2. Step 2

    Create WorkspaceStoreTests.swift and start with three tests: sample tasks are added only once, a new task goes to the top and undo and redo work, and a blank title is rejected. #require stops a test early when a value it depends on is missing.

    WorkspaceStoreTests.swift

Section 2

Test the Tools Directly

The toolbox returns a ToolResult, so you can check both halves of every tool call, the sentence the model would read and the activity the UI would show, without a model.

  1. Step 1

    Create AgentFixture.swift with makeStore() and a collect(_:) helper that gathers every event from an engine's stream.

    AgentFixture.swift
    1import Foundation2@testable import WorkspaceAssistant3 4/// A store over in-memory storage with the six sample tasks.5@MainActor6func makeStore(extra: [TaskItem] = []) -> WorkspaceStore {7    WorkspaceStore(8        repository: InMemoryTaskRepository(),9        preferencesStore: InMemoryPreferencesStore(),10        seed: SampleData.tasks() + extra11    )12}13 14@MainActor15extension WorkspaceStore {16    func task(titled title: String) -> TaskItem? { tasks.first { $0.title == title } }17}18 19/// Collects every event from an engine response.20@MainActor21func collect(_ stream: AsyncThrowingStream<AssistantEvent, any Error>) async throws -> [AssistantEvent] {22    var events: [AssistantEvent] = []23    for try await event in stream { events.append(event) }24    return events25}26 27extension [AssistantEvent] {28    var activities: [ToolActivity] { compactMap { if case let .toolCalled(activity) = $0 { activity } else { nil } } }29    var finalText: String? { compactMap { if case let .completed(text) = $0 { text } else { nil } }.last }30}

  2. Step 2

    Create WorkspaceToolboxTests.swift. The important tests are the honest ones: an already-high task reports no change, an unknown task is a truthful noMatch, and an ambiguous query lists its candidates.

    WorkspaceToolboxTests.swift

Section 3

Test the View Model with a Fake Engine

AssistantViewModel only knows the AssistantEngine protocol, so a fake engine lets a test decide exactly which events arrive, and when.

  1. Step 1

    Create FakeEngine.swift. emit(_:) pushes an event and finish(throwing:) ends the stream. settle() lets queued main-actor work run before the test checks the result.

    FakeEngine.swift
    1import Foundation2@testable import WorkspaceAssistant3 4/// A controllable engine: tests push events and finish the stream manually.5@MainActor6final class FakeEngine: AssistantEngine {7    var availability: AssistantAvailability = .available8    var simulationReason: AssistantUnavailableReason?9    var isResponding = false10    private(set) var prompts: [String] = []11    private(set) var resetCount = 012    private var continuation: AsyncThrowingStream<AssistantEvent, any Error>.Continuation?13    private(set) var wasTerminated = false14 15    func send(_ prompt: String) -> AsyncThrowingStream<AssistantEvent, any Error> {16        prompts.append(prompt)17        isResponding = true18        return AsyncThrowingStream { continuation in19            self.continuation = continuation20            continuation.onTermination = { _ in21                Task { @MainActor in self.wasTerminated = true }22            }23        }24    }25 26    func emit(_ event: AssistantEvent) { continuation?.yield(event) }27 28    func finish(throwing error: (any Error)? = nil) {29        isResponding = false30        continuation?.finish(throwing: error)31        continuation = nil32    }33 34    func reset() async { resetCount += 1 }35    func prewarm() async {}36}37 38/// Lets queued main-actor tasks run.39@MainActor40func settle() async {41    for _ in 0..<5 { await Task.yield() }42    try? await Task.sleep(for: .milliseconds(20))43}

  2. Step 2

    Create AssistantViewModelTests.swift. It checks streaming, a tool call that arrives late being placed before the reply, cancelling, errors becoming notices, and clearing that never touches tasks. Press ⌘U to run all the tests in seconds.

    AssistantViewModelTests.swift

AssistantViewModel10 11    init() {12        model = AssistantViewModel(engine: engine)13    }14 15    let activity = ToolActivity(kind: .setPriority, parameters: [.task(title: "Refactor Network Layer", id: UUID()), .priority(.high)], outcome: .success)16 17    @Test func sendTrimsAndAppendsUserMessage() {18        model.draft = "  Switch to Board view \n\n"19        model.send()20        #expect(engine.prompts == ["Switch to Board view"])21        #expect(model.draft.isEmpty)22        #expect(model.phase == .responding)23        #expect(model.items.first?.content == .user("Switch to Board view"))24    }25 26    @Test func blankDraftIsIgnored() {27        model.draft = " \n "28        model.send()29        #expect(engine.prompts.isEmpty)30        #expect(model.items.isEmpty)31    }32 33    @Test func secondSendWhileRespondingIsIgnored() {34        model.draft = "one"35        model.send()36        model.draft = "two"37        model.send()38        #expect(engine.prompts == ["one"])39        #expect(model.draft == "two")40    }41 42    @Test func streamsToolCallsThenText() async {43        model.draft = "prioritise network"44        model.send()45        engine.emit(.toolCalled(activity))46        engine.emit(.partialText("Done"))47        await settle()48        #expect(model.items.count == 3)49        #expect(model.items[1].content == .action(activity))50        #expect(model.items[2].content == .assistant("Done", isStreaming: true))51        #expect(model.lastActivity == activity)52 53        engine.emit(.partialText("Done — prioritised."))54        engine.emit(.completed("Done — prioritised."))55        engine.finish()56        await settle()57        #expect(model.items.last?.content == .assistant("Done — prioritised.", isStreaming: false))58        #expect(model.phase == .idle)59    }60 61    @Test func lateToolCallIsInsertedBeforeStreamingReply() async {62        model.draft = "x"63        model.send()64
